he doesn't say 'I'll make you happy.'
He says —
"I can't promise it'll all be good from here.
I can't promise we won't fight over stupid things again.
But I can promise one thing:
I'll stay by your side.
Whatever breaks, I'll fix it."

The reason this line wrecks people
is because it's not really a proposal —
it's closer to an apology.

A grown-up promise isn't 'we won't fight.'
It's 'even if we do, I'm not leaving.'
Grown-up love isn't 'I'll give you a perfect life.'
It's 'the imperfect parts — I'll figure them out.'

It takes a certain age to finally see it:
the person who'll sit there and fix things with you
is worth so much more
than the person who keeps promising 'nothing will ever break.'

One is just talking.
The other is actually planning to stay.
en.editorNote: For the friend on the fence about a relationship — the question isn't whether something broke, it's whether the other person will help fix it
variations: Advanced: flip it on yourself too — are you the one who stays and fixes? Both sides need to be, or the repair doesn't hold

items.sourceNote: POPBEE 2026治癒系韓劇台詞推薦，「情緒生病像感冒一樣正常」原創改編

zh-tw.content:
近幾年韓劇最大的進步，
是它終於敢這樣寫：
「情緒生病，跟感冒一樣正常。
感冒要吃藥、要休息、要跟公司請假，
那情緒生病為什麼不行？」

小時候被教的是——
「不要哭」、「忍一下就好」、
「想開一點」、「別人比你慘多了」。

結果長大之後，
我們變成一群很會處理感冒、
但完全不知道怎麼處理情緒的人。

胃痛你會掛號，
但心痛你會自己撐三個月。
發燒你會請病假，
但焦慮到睡不著你照樣去上班。

韓劇現在敢拍這些，
是因為它知道——
觀眾需要有人替他們講一次：
「你那個跟矯情無關，也跟脆弱無關，
那是真的不舒服。
值得被當一回事。」

所以今天如果你有點不對勁，
不要急著解釋「應該還好」。
先承認它，
再決定要不要去處理它。

感冒不會因為你假裝沒事就自己好。
情緒也是。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個明明很不舒服、卻一直說「我沒事」的朋友——你不用假裝堅強，先承認再說
variations: 進階版：今天為自己「請一次情緒病假」，可以是半小時、一杯咖啡、一段散步——讓自己正式承認「我現在有點不行」

en.content:
The biggest shift in K-dramas the last few years
is they finally have the guts to write this:
"Getting sick emotionally is as normal as a cold.
You take medicine for a cold, you rest, you call out from work —
so why not for this?"

As kids we were taught —
'don't cry,' 'just push through,'
'try to think positive,' 'other people have it worse.'

So we grew up into a generation
that handles colds very well
and has absolutely no idea what to do with emotions.

Stomach pain — you book a doctor.
Heart pain — you white-knuckle it for three months.
Fever — you call out.
Anxiety so bad you can't sleep — you still go to work.

K-dramas can write this now
because they know —
the audience needs someone to say it once for them:
'What you're feeling isn't dramatic, isn't weakness.
It's real discomfort.
It deserves to be taken seriously.'

So today, if something feels off,
don't rush to explain it away with 'I'm probably fine.'
Acknowledge it first.
Then decide what to do about it.

A cold doesn't go away because you pretend it isn't there.
Neither does this.
en.editorNote: For the friend who's clearly not okay but keeps saying 'I'm fine' — you don't have to perform strength, start by admitting it
variations: Advanced: take one 'emotional sick day' today — half an hour, a coffee, a walk. Make it official: 'I'm not okay right now, and that's allowed'

items.sourceNote: 2025年話題韓劇親情主題討論，母女關係台詞觀察，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
今年最戳人的韓劇台詞，
不是男女主角在雨中告白，
而是媽媽對長大的女兒說：

「我這輩子最大的成就，
不是把妳養大，
是讓妳變成一個
不需要為了討我開心
而委屈自己的人。」

看到這句的時候，
你會突然很想打電話回家，
但又不知道要說什麼，
最後只傳了一句：「在幹嘛？」

那句「在幹嘛」，
其實是「我想你了」的台灣版翻譯。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個明明很想家、卻只會傳「在幹嘛」給媽媽的朋友——這就是我們表達想念的方式
variations: 進階版：今天真的打一通電話回家，不用有事，就聊三分鐘——你會發現掛掉之後心裡有個地方變暖了

en.content:
The K-drama line that wrecked everyone this year
wasn't a rain-soaked confession between leads.
It was a mother telling her grown daughter:

"The biggest thing I ever did
wasn't raising you.
It was raising you into someone
who doesn't have to shrink herself
just to keep me happy."

The second you read that,
you want to call home —
but you don't know what to say,
so you just text: "what are you up to?"

That "what are you up to"
is the translated version of "I miss you."
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who clearly misses home but only ever texts their mom 'what are you up to' — that's how we say it
variations: Advanced: actually call home today. No reason needed, just three minutes. You'll notice a spot inside you warms up after you hang up.

items.sourceNote: Dcard韓劇板字幕追劇行為討論，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
看韓劇看久了會出現一種後遺症：

你開始覺得自己聽得懂韓文。

字幕都還沒跑出來，
你就跟著喊「歐摩」、「真的假的」、「我愛你」，
然後很滿意地點點頭，
覺得自己根本不需要字幕。

直到字幕真的消失三秒鐘，
你瞬間清醒，
意識到自己其實一個字都沒聽懂，
只是把語氣背起來而已。

「會的韓文」和「會背的語氣」，
是兩回事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個追劇追到以為自己會韓文、嘴上一直「歐摩歐摩」的朋友——讓他笑著認清現實
variations: 更慘的版本：你跟同事自信地說「我看韓劇學了不少韓文」，結果去韓國旅遊時，唯一派上用場的只有「卡姆撒哈密達」

en.content:
Watch enough K-dramas and you develop a side effect:

you start believing you understand Korean.

Before the subtitles even load,
you're already saying "omo," "jinjja," "saranghae"
right along with them,
nodding to yourself,
convinced you don't even need the captions.

Then the subtitles actually drop for three seconds,
and you snap back to reality:
you understood literally nothing.
You just memorized the tone.

"Knowing Korean"
and "memorizing the intonation"
are not the same skill.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who thinks binge-watching taught them Korean and won't stop saying 'omo omo' — let them laugh and face the truth
variations: Worse version: you confidently tell coworkers 'I picked up a lot of Korean from dramas,' then on your Korea trip the only phrase you actually use is 'kamsahamnida.'

items.sourceNote: UDN女子漾韓劇人生哲理金句整理，職場與成長主題，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇裡有一句話一直被截圖轉發：

「不要因為害怕受傷，
就提前把自己關起來。
你以為這樣很安全，
其實你只是錯過了
所有本來會發生的好事。」

聽起來很雞湯，
但仔細想想——
你拒絕的那場聚會、
沒去面試的那份工作、
不敢傳出去的那則訊息，
哪一個不是因為「怕」？

安全感有時候沒在保護你，
它把你困在原地。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個總是用「我這樣比較安全」當理由、其實是在逃避的朋友——溫柔但要讓他聽進去
variations: 進階版：今天做一件你「有點怕但其實想做」的小事就好——報名那堂課、傳那則訊息、舉手說那句話。怕和想，可以同時存在。

en.content:
There's a K-drama line that keeps getting screenshotted:

"Don't lock yourself away in advance
just because you're scared of getting hurt.
You think it keeps you safe,
but really you're just missing
every good thing that was supposed to happen."

Sounds like a fortune cookie,
until you actually think about it —
the gathering you turned down,
the job you didn't interview for,
the text you never dared to send.
Which of those wasn't fear?

Sometimes safety isn't protecting you.
It's just keeping you stuck.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who keeps saying 'this is safer for me' when they're really just avoiding — gentle, but make it land
variations: Advanced: do one small thing today that scares you a little but you actually want — sign up, send the text, raise your hand. Scared and wanting can coexist.

items.sourceNote: POPBEE韓劇追劇時間管理現象觀察，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
追韓劇的人都很擅長一種數學：

凌晨一點，看完一集。
你心想：「最後一集了，看完就睡。」

結果片尾留了個超大的伏筆，
你大喊：「不行，這怎麼睡得著。」

於是「再一集」變成「再三集」，
「就睡」變成「天亮」。

隔天上班頂著黑眼圈，
同事問你怎麼了，
你只能說：「沒事，就……劇情需要。」

世界上最遠的距離，
是「最後一集」和「真正睡覺」之間。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每次都說「看完這集就睡」、然後追到天亮的朋友——他需要被點名
variations: 進階版：今晚設一個真的會響的鬧鐘，到點就暫停，把伏筆留到明天——相信我，劇情明天還在，但你的黑眼圈不會自己消失

en.content:
K-drama fans are weirdly good at one kind of math:

1 AM, you finish an episode.
You think: "last one, then I sleep."

Then the credits drop a massive cliffhanger
and you yell: "nope, no way I'm sleeping after that."

So "one more" becomes "three more,"
and "then sleep" becomes "then sunrise."

Next day at work, raccoon eyes,
a coworker asks what happened,
and all you can say is: "nothing, it's just… the plot needed it."

The longest distance in the world
is between "last episode"
and "actually going to sleep."
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who says 'just this episode then bed' and watches till sunrise every single time — call them out
variations: Advanced: set an alarm that actually goes off tonight, pause when it rings, save the cliffhanger for tomorrow. Trust me, the plot will still be there. Your eye bags won't fix themselves.

items.sourceNote: beauty321韓劇友情主題場景整理，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇最會拍的，其實不是愛情，
是那種一句話都不用說的友情。

你心情很差，
朋友沒問你怎麼了，
只是默默放了一碗熱湯在你面前，
坐在旁邊陪你發呆。

劇裡那句台詞是這樣的：
「我不一定懂你發生了什麼，
但我可以坐在這裡，
直到你想說話為止。」

真正的陪伴，
從來不是給建議，
是讓你知道：你難過的時候，
旁邊有個位子，一直是你的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個總是默默陪你、什麼都不問的朋友——讓他知道那碗湯你一直記得
variations: 進階版：今天主動坐到那個看起來不太好的朋友旁邊，不用問，不用給建議，就陪著——有時候在場本身就是答案

en.content:
What K-dramas film best isn't romance.
It's the kind of friendship that needs no words.

You're in a terrible mood,
and your friend doesn't ask what's wrong.
They just quietly set a bowl of hot soup in front of you
and sit beside you while you stare into space.

The line in the show goes:
"I might not understand what happened to you,
but I can sit right here
until you feel like talking."

Real company
was never about giving advice.
It's letting someone know:
when you're hurting, there's a seat next to you,
and it's always been yours.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who quietly stays with you and never pries — let them know you still remember that bowl of soup
variations: Advanced: today, go sit next to the friend who seems off. Don't ask, don't advise, just be there. Sometimes showing up is the whole answer.

items.sourceNote: POPBEE 2026治癒系韓劇台詞推薦，平凡人生主題，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
長大之後才發現，
光是把日子過成「普通」，
就已經用掉我全部的力氣。

小時候以為長大會變很厲害，
結果現在的目標是：
準時起床、好好吃飯、
帳單不要遲繳、別在深夜emo太久。

韓劇裡有句話我記了好久：
「承認自己只想當個平凡人，
一點都不丟臉。」

不是每個人都要發光，
有時候能穩穩地活著，
就已經很了不起了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個總覺得自己「不夠好」、把普通生活活成壓力的朋友——告訴他活著本身就值得被肯定
variations: 進階版：今天先不要逼自己變得更好，只要把今天好好過完就夠了——明天的你，會謝謝今天沒有崩潰的你

en.content:
Growing up, I figured out
that just keeping life "normal"
eats up every bit of energy I have.

As a kid I thought I'd turn out impressive.
Now my actual goals are:
wake up on time, eat real meals,
pay bills before they're late,
and not spiral at 2 AM.

There's a K-drama line I've held onto:
"There's nothing shameful
about admitting you just want to be ordinary."

Not everyone has to shine.
Sometimes just staying steady, staying alive,
is already a huge deal.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who feels 'not good enough' and turns ordinary life into pressure — remind them that simply being here counts
variations: Advanced: today, don't force yourself to be better. Just get through today. Tomorrow-you will thank today-you for not falling apart.

items.sourceNote: POPBEE 2026治癒系韓劇台詞，幸福主導權主題，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇教會我一件很殘酷但很真的事：

你的快樂，只有你自己給得起。

等別人記得你的生日才覺得被愛、
等對方先傳訊息才敢開心、
等老闆一句肯定才覺得自己有用——

你把幸福的開關，
交到了一個不一定會幫你打開的人手上。

劇裡那句話是這樣說的：
「不要把決定你快不快樂的權力，
交給別人。」

從今天開始，
那個開關，自己拿回來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個總是在等別人給自己快樂、卻常常失望的朋友——提醒他幸福的主導權一直在自己手上
variations: 進階版：今天做一件「只為了讓自己開心」的小事，不用問別人意見，不用等任何人同意——那叫把開關拿回來

en.content:
K-dramas taught me something brutal but true:

Your happiness is something only you can hand yourself.

Waiting for someone to remember your birthday to feel loved,
waiting for them to text first before you let yourself be happy,
waiting for your boss's approval to feel useful —

you've handed the switch to your own joy
to a person who might never flip it on.

The line in the show goes:
"Don't give anyone else
the power to decide whether you're happy."

Starting today,
take that switch back.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who keeps waiting on others for happiness and keeps getting let down — remind them the controls were always theirs
variations: Advanced: today do one small thing purely to make yourself happy. Don't ask for opinions, don't wait for permission. That's taking the switch back.

items.sourceNote: Korean Binge 韓劇愛情台詞整理，選擇你主題，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇裡最讓人心動的告白，
從來不是「我愛你」三個字，
是那種「我選你」的篤定：

「如果有一天，
我必須做一個很殘忍的選擇，
我會選你。
因為失去我愛的人，
比失去我自己還要痛。」

愛你，不是激情上頭的衝動，
是在所有理智都清醒的時候，
還是把你放在最前面。

那不是一時的心動，
那是一種——「無論如何都是你」的決定。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個正在猶豫要不要認真對待一段感情的人——真正的愛是清醒時依然選擇你
variations: 進階版：愛情裡最浪漫的不是「我好喜歡你」，是吵完架、累到不行、看清彼此缺點之後，還願意說一句「明天還要一起」

en.content:
The most heart-stopping confessions in K-dramas
were never the words "I love you."
It's that quiet certainty of "I choose you":

"If the day ever comes
when I have to make a cruel choice,
I'll choose you.
Because losing the person I love
hurts more than losing myself."

Loving you isn't a rush of passion.
It's choosing you first
even when every rational part of me is wide awake.

That's not a fleeting flutter.
That's a decision —
"no matter what, it's you."
en.editorNote: Send to someone hesitating over whether to take a relationship seriously — real love is still choosing you when the head is clear
variations: Advanced: the most romantic thing in love isn't 'I really like you.' It's saying 'let's do tomorrow together' after the fight, after the exhaustion, after seeing each other's flaws clearly.

items.sourceNote: UDN女子漾《低谷醫生》治癒金句整理，倒下休息主題，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇裡有一句話，
是給每個撐到快斷氣的人聽的：

「既然都倒下了，
那就先躺著休息一下吧。」

我們從小被教的是：
跌倒要馬上爬起來、
哭完要馬上振作、
累了也要假裝沒事。

但其實啊，
倒下算不上失敗，
那是身體在替你喊停。

地板沒有那麼可怕，
躺一下，看看天花板，
等你想站起來的時候再站，
沒有人在計時。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個明明已經很累、卻還在硬撐的人——告訴他停下來不是認輸，是補給
variations: 進階版：你不需要每天都很努力。有些日子，把自己餵飽、好好睡一覺，就已經是這一天最了不起的成就了

en.content:
There's a line in K-dramas
meant for everyone running on empty:

"Since you've already fallen down,
just lie there and rest for a bit."

We were raised to believe:
get up the second you trip,
snap out of it the second you stop crying,
pretend you're fine even when you're wrecked.

But here's the thing —
falling isn't failure.
It's your body calling a timeout for you.

The floor isn't that scary.
Lie down, look at the ceiling,
get up when you actually want to.
Nobody's running a clock.
en.editorNote: Send to someone who's clearly exhausted but still pushing through — let them know stopping isn't quitting, it's refueling
variations: Advanced: you don't have to crush it every single day. Some days, feeding yourself and getting real sleep is the most impressive thing you'll do.

items.sourceNote: Korean Binge 韓劇愛情台詞整理，思念與飢餓比喻，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇把「想你」這件事，
寫得連你自己都分不清楚：

「我是因為餓了才想你，
還是因為想你才覺得餓？」

喜歡一個人到某個程度，
會出現一種很荒謬的混亂——
吃飯想到他、
走路想到他、
明明在忙，腦袋還是自己飄過去。

你開始懷疑
自己是不是身體出了什麼問題，
後來才發現，
那不是毛病，
那是喜歡。

而且是
連肚子餓都怪到他頭上的那種喜歡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個最近一直心不在焉、嘴上不承認自己戀愛了的朋友——幫他確診
variations: 進階版：判斷你是不是真的喜歡一個人，很簡單——看到好笑的東西，第一個想分享的人是誰，答案就藏在那裡

en.content:
A K-drama wrote "missing you"
in a way that even confuses the person feeling it:

"Am I thinking of you because I'm hungry,
or am I hungry because I'm thinking of you?"

When you like someone past a certain point,
this ridiculous kind of confusion shows up —
you think of them while eating,
while walking,
your brain drifts off to them mid-task.

You start wondering
if something's medically wrong with you.
Then you realize
it's not a glitch.
It's a crush.

The kind
where you even blame your hunger on them.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who's been distracted lately and won't admit they've caught feelings — give them the diagnosis
variations: Advanced: an easy test for whether you actually like someone — when something funny happens, who's the first person you want to tell? The answer's hiding right there.

items.sourceNote: Pinkvilla韓劇金句，自我價值與愛得多主題，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇講過一句話，
戳破了一個我們從小被教的迷思：

「愛一個人愛得比對方多，
不是丟臉的事，
那是值得驕傲的事。」

我們總被提醒：
不要先告白、
不要先已讀回、
不要讓對方知道你比較在乎，
好像先動心的人就輸了。

但其實能毫無保留地喜歡一個人，
是一種很多人一輩子都學不會的勇敢。

你不是輸了，
你只是比較敢。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個總覺得「先喜歡上就輸了」、不敢先付出的朋友——告訴他先動心不丟臉
variations: 進階版：愛得多的人不是傻，是他知道感情不是比賽，沒有誰要贏過誰

en.content:
A K-drama said something
that shatters a myth we're taught young:

"Loving someone more than they love you
isn't embarrassing.
It's something to be proud of."

We're always warned:
don't confess first,
don't reply too fast,
don't let them see you care more —
as if whoever falls first loses.

But being able to like someone
with nothing held back
is a kind of courage most people never learn.

You didn't lose.
You were just braver.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who thinks 'whoever falls first loses' and is scared to give first — remind them falling first isn't shameful
variations: Advanced: the one who loves more isn't a fool. They just figured out love isn't a contest where someone has to win.

items.sourceNote: KORB韓劇愛情台詞，時間感受主題，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇有一句台詞，
短到不行，卻很可怕地準：

「沒有你的那三十幾年，
我過得飛快；
認識你之後的每一天，
卻長得像一輩子。」

喜歡一個人最明顯的證據，
不是心跳加速，
是你的時間感壞掉了——

等他回訊息的十分鐘像一小時，
和他在一起的三小時像三分鐘。

如果你最近覺得時間怪怪的，
那可能不是你的錯，
是某個人住進了你的日子裡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個最近老說「跟某人在一起時間過超快」的朋友——幫他確認一下他是不是喜歡上了
variations: 反過來的版本：如果跟一個人在一起，你一直偷看時間，那也是答案，只是是另一種答案

en.content:
There's a K-drama line
so short it shouldn't work, but it's scarily accurate:

"The thirty-odd years before you
went by in a blink;
every day since I met you
feels like it lasts forever."

The clearest proof you like someone
isn't the racing heartbeat.
It's that your sense of time breaks —

ten minutes waiting for their text feels like an hour,
three hours with them feels like three minutes.

If time's been feeling strange lately,
it might not be your fault.
Someone just moved into your days.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who keeps saying 'time flies when I'm with this person' — help them confirm whether they've caught feelings
variations: The flip side: if you keep sneaking glances at the clock when you're with someone, that's an answer too — just a different one.

items.sourceNote: When Life Gives You Tangerines（苦盡柑來遇見你），大人也會被燙傷主題，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
小時候以為，長大之後，
手會長繭、心也會長繭，
再痛的事都能笑著扛過去。

結果長大了才發現：
手是長繭了，
心一點都沒有。

每一次受傷還是一樣痛，
每一次失望還是一樣難過，
只是我學會了
在別人面前裝沒事。

原來長大不會讓你不痛，
只是長大之後，
沒有人能替你喊痛了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個總是把「我沒事」掛在嘴邊、但你知道他其實很累的朋友——讓他知道有人看得見
variations: 更貼心的版本：你不用在我面前裝沒事，至少在我這裡，你可以喊痛

en.content:
As a kid, I thought that once you grew up,
your hands would callous over,
and so would your heart —
that nothing would really hurt anymore.

Then I grew up and found out:
the hands got calloused, sure.
The heart never did.

Every wound still stings the same.
Every letdown still aches the same.
The only thing I learned
was how to look fine in front of people.

Turns out growing up doesn't stop the pain.
It just means no one
gets to flinch on your behalf anymore.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who always says 'I'm fine' but you can tell they're worn out — let them know someone sees it
variations: The softer version: you don't have to look fine in front of me. With me, at least, you're allowed to say it hurts.

items.sourceNote: When Life Gives You Tangerines，父母與孩子各自掛念主題，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇裡有一句，看完整個人安靜下來：

「父母一輩子都在想，
自己沒能給孩子的那些；
孩子一輩子都在記，
自己沒能得到的那些。」

所以一邊覺得虧欠，
一邊覺得委屈，
兩個人明明最愛彼此，
卻常常用最笨的方式錯過。

下次回家，
別急著翻舊帳，
他們給的，
其實一直比你記得的多。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個跟爸媽容易吵、但其實很愛他們的朋友——提醒他別只記得沒得到的
variations: 行動版：今天打通電話回家，什麼事都不用講，就說一句「我最近很好，你們別擔心」

en.content:
A K-drama line that made the whole room go quiet:

"Parents spend their whole lives
dwelling on what they couldn't give.
Children spend their whole lives
dwelling on what they didn't get."

So one side carries guilt,
the other carries hurt,
and the two people who love each other most
keep missing each other the clumsiest way.

Next time you go home,
don't reach for the old grievances.
They gave more
than you remember.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who argues with their parents easily but loves them deeply — a nudge to stop counting only what they didn't get
variations: The action version: call home today. Don't bring anything up. Just say, 'I've been doing well, don't worry about me.'

items.sourceNote: When Life Gives You Tangerines，撐住就能再呼吸主題，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇裡有一段話，
適合在很撐不住的那天聽：

「總有一天，
日子會難到你覺得走不下去。
那種時候，
不要躺著不動，
要用盡全力掙扎——
告訴自己：我不會死，
我一定要活著撐過去。
然後你就會發現，
你又能呼吸了。」

低潮沒有叫你堅強，
它叫你別停手。
撐住，
下一口氣就在前面。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個正在硬撐、快要放棄的朋友——不用講道理，把這段話給他就好
variations: 簡短版：你現在覺得喘不過氣，是因為你還在水裡掙扎，這代表你還沒放棄——這樣很好

en.content:
There's a K-drama line
made for the days you can barely hold on:

"One day life will get so hard
you'll feel like you can't go on.
When that day comes,
don't just lie there.
Struggle with everything you've got —
tell yourself: I won't die,
I have to survive this no matter what.
And then you'll realize
you can breathe again."

A low point isn't asking you to be strong.
It's asking you not to let go.
Hold on.
The next breath is right there.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who's white-knuckling it and about to give up — skip the advice, just give them this
variations: The short version: if you feel like you can't breathe right now, it's because you're still fighting in the water. That means you haven't given up. That's good.

items.sourceNote: Queen of Tears（淚之女王），身體記得怎麼游泳比喻愛，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇有一段比喻，
適合送給「覺得自己再也不會愛了」的人：

「小時候學會游泳，
之後幾十年沒下水，
但只要再跳進去，
身體還是會浮起來。
你以為全忘了，
其實身體一直記得。

愛也一樣。
你以為自己忘了怎麼愛，
但只要真的投入，
你的心會自己想起來。」

別怕你受過傷就不會愛了，
那只是你還沒跳下水而已。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個經歷過很傷的分手、說「我大概不會再愛了」的朋友——告訴他不是不會，只是還沒開始
variations: 鼓勵版：你不是壞掉了，你只是還沒遇到那個讓你願意再跳下水的人
更短：你以為忘了怎麼愛，其實只是太久沒愛——心比你想的還記得

en.content:
A K-drama uses this metaphor,
perfect for anyone who thinks they'll never love again:

"We learn to swim as kids.
Then we don't touch water for decades.
But jump back in,
and the body still floats.
You think you forgot it all —
your body never did.

Love is the same.
You think you've forgotten how,
but once you really dive in,
your heart remembers on its own."

Don't fear that getting hurt means you can't love anymore.
It just means you haven't jumped back in yet.
en.editorNote: Send to a friend who went through a brutal breakup and says 'I probably won't love again' — it's not that you can't, you just haven't started
variations: Encouraging version: you're not broken. You just haven't met the person who makes you want to jump back in.
Shorter: you think you forgot how to love. You've just gone too long without it. Your heart remembers more than you do.

items.sourceNote: 淚之女王婚姻與留下來主題台詞，愛情不是甜言蜜語而是一起撐過，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇有一句，
戳破了所有人對愛情的幻想：

「愛不是一直甜甜的、
在耳邊講好聽的話。
愛，是兩個人一起撐過那段很痛的日子。
是選擇留下來，而不是轉身就走。」

熱戀的時候誰都會講情話，
真正的愛是——
吵完架、累到不行、什麼都不想說的那天，
你還是沒有走。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個以為「不再心動就是不愛了」的朋友——愛不是一直心動，是難的時候還願意留下來
variations: 更短：會講情話的人很多，願意在最難那天還留下來的人，很少
戀人版：我沒辦法保證每天都甜甜的，但我可以保證，再難我都不會先走

en.content:
A K-drama line
that dismantles everyone's fantasy of love:

"Love isn't always sweet,
whispering pretty words in your ear.
Love is two people enduring the painful days together.
It's choosing to stay
instead of turning around and leaving."

Anyone can say sweet things in the honeymoon phase.
Real love is —
after the fight, when you're exhausted
and have nothing left to say,
you still didn't walk out.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who thinks 'no more butterflies means no more love' — love isn't constant fluttering, it's staying when things get hard
variations: Shorter: plenty of people can say sweet things. Few are willing to stay on the hardest day.
For a partner: I can't promise every day will be sweet. But I can promise I won't be the one who leaves first.

items.sourceNote: Lovely Runner跨越時空找到你主題台詞，每一世都會愛你，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇最浪漫的告白之一，
不是「我愛你」，
而是這句：

「不管是哪一世，
我都會找到你。
每一世，我都會愛上你。」

聽起來很誇張，
但它戳中的是一種很深的渴望——
不是被愛一次，
是被一個人，
用一輩子、甚至好幾輩子的決心愛著。

我們要的從來不是轟轟烈烈，
是「我認定就是你」的那份篤定。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個值得你認定的人——或那個一直懷疑自己值不值得被好好愛的朋友
variations: 更短：我不要愛你一陣子，我要認定你一輩子
土味版：別人問我要找幾世的緣分，我說不用算，每一世翻到你那頁我都停下來

en.content:
One of the most romantic confessions in K-dramas
isn't "I love you."
It's this:

"No matter what lifetime it is,
I'll find you.
In every lifetime, I'll love you."

It sounds over the top,
but it hits a very deep wish —
not to be loved once,
but to be loved by someone
with the resolve of a whole life,
or even several.

What we actually want isn't fireworks.
It's the certainty of "it's you, I've decided."
en.editorNote: Send to the person worth deciding on — or the friend who keeps doubting whether they deserve to be loved well
variations: Shorter: I don't want to love you for a while. I want to be sure of you for a lifetime.
Cheesy version: Ask me how many lifetimes of fate I'm looking for? Don't bother counting — every lifetime, I stop on your page.

items.sourceNote: 今生也請多指教人生選擇主題台詞，現在是無數選擇的結果，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇有一句，
講透了「現在的你」是怎麼來的：

「所謂的人生，
每一個瞬間都塞滿了選擇。
我此刻所經歷的一切，
都是我過去做過的
無數個選擇，加起來的結果。」

所以別再說「我怎麼會走到這一步」，
命運沒有把你推到這裡，
是你自己一步一步選來的。

好消息是——
下一步，也還是你選。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個覺得人生卡住、怪命運怪環境的朋友——提醒他下一個選擇權還在自己手上
variations: 更短：你現在的生活，是過去所有選擇的總和；想換結果，先換選擇
鼓勵版：走到這裡的是過去的選擇，往哪走，還是你現在說了算

en.content:
A K-drama line
that explains exactly how 'current you' got here:

"Life is packed with choices
in every single moment.
Everything I'm living through right now
is the sum of
countless choices I made in the past."

So stop saying "how did I end up here."
Fate didn't shove you to this spot.
You chose your way here, one step at a time.

The good news —
the next step is still yours to choose.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who feels stuck and blames fate or circumstances — remind them the next choice is still in their hands
variations: Shorter: your life right now is the sum of past choices. Want a different result? Change the choices.
Encouraging version: past choices got you here. Where you go next is still yours to call.

items.sourceNote: 韓劇時間與離別主題台詞，趁變成遺憾前說出口，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇有一句，
聽完會想立刻拿起手機打電話：

「時間會走，
所以時間帶來離別，
也因此，時間總是留下遺憾。

如果你愛一個人，
現在就說吧——
趁這個忙到不行的瞬間，
還沒變成遺憾之前。」

我們總以為「以後再說」，
但「以後」這兩個字，
吃掉了人這輩子最多想說的話。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個總把「改天再聯絡」掛嘴邊、卻一直沒行動的朋友——提醒他現在就打那通電話
variations: 更短：想說的話別留到以後，因為「以後」常常不會來
行動版：看完這句，去傳訊息給那個你一直想聯絡卻拖著的人

en.content:
A K-drama line
that makes you want to grab your phone and call someone:

"Time moves on,
so time brings goodbyes,
and because of that, time always leaves regret.

If you love someone,
say it now —
in this impossibly busy moment,
before it turns into regret."

We always think "I'll say it later."
But that one word, "later,"
has eaten more unsaid things
than anything else in a person's life.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who always says 'let's catch up sometime' but never does — tell them to make the call now
variations: Shorter: don't save what you want to say for later — 'later' often never comes.
Action version: after reading this, go text the person you've been meaning to reach but kept putting off.

items.sourceNote: When Life Gives You Tangerines聖誕樹比喻自我價值，無論放哪都閃閃發光，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇有一句很溫柔的話，
送給那個總覺得自己不夠好的人：

「一棵樹，不管被放在哪，
都會好好做它自己。
就算這棵聖誕樹被擺在沒人來的地下室、
或一間沒人光顧的小店角落，
它一樣閃閃發光，
一樣讓人看了心動。」

你的價值，
從來不是因為「有沒有人看見」才存在。
你發光，
是因為你本來就會發光。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個覺得自己沒被看見、開始懷疑自己價值的朋友——提醒他發光是天生的，跟有沒有人看無關
variations: 更短：你會發光，不是因為有人看；沒人看的時候，你一樣亮著
鼓勵版：別因為現在沒人看見就把自己的光關掉，對的人來的時候，要看得到你

en.content:
A gentle K-drama line
for anyone who keeps feeling like they're not enough:

"A tree just does its job
no matter where you put it.
Whether a Christmas tree sits
in a basement no one visits
or a corner of a shop no one walks into,
it's always sparkling.
It still makes your heart pound."

Your worth
was never conditional on being seen.
You shine
because shining is just what you do.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who feels unseen and is starting to doubt their worth — remind them shining is innate, not dependent on an audience
variations: Shorter: you don't shine because someone's watching. When no one is, you're still lit up.
Encouraging version: don't switch off your light just because no one's looking right now. The right people need to be able to find you.

items.sourceNote: When Life Gives You Tangerines自我與愛情並存的台詞，深愛對方也深愛自己，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇裡有一句台詞，
戳破了很多人對愛情的誤會：

「我是真的很愛你。
但我也一樣，很愛我自己。」

年輕的時候以為，
愛一個人就是把自己整個交出去，
對方的喜怒哀樂，變成你全部的天氣。

後來才懂，
能好好愛你的人，
是那個沒有把自己弄丟的人。
你還在，
愛才有人可以站著。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個在感情裡習慣把自己縮到很小、只剩對方的朋友——提醒他，先把自己接回來
variations: 更短：愛你，不代表我要弄丟我自己；我都在，這份愛才站得住
提醒版：對方再重要，也不能變成你全部的天氣；你得替自己留一塊晴天

en.content:
There's a K-drama line
that quietly corrects how a lot of us understand love:

"I do love you, deeply.
But I love myself just as deeply, too."

When you're young you think
loving someone means handing yourself over whole,
letting their moods become your entire weather.

Later you learn:
the person who can love you well
is the one who didn't lose themselves to do it.
You have to still be there
for the love to have somewhere to stand.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who shrinks themselves down to nothing in relationships until only the other person is left — remind them to bring themselves back
variations: Shorter: loving you doesn't mean losing me. The love only holds up while I'm still here.
Reminder version: no matter how much they matter, they can't become your entire weather. Keep some clear sky for yourself.

items.sourceNote: Our Unwritten Seoul人生是一本要自己填寫的筆記本，空白頁是開始不是結束，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇有一句話，
送給站在空白人生前、覺得自己卡住的人：

「我一直以為人生是一本書，
翻到最後一頁就結束。
後來才發現，
它其實是一本筆記本，
每一頁，都要我自己寫上去。

所以遇到空白的那一頁，
不是結束，
是還沒寫的開始。」

你現在的空白，
不是沒有故事，
是輪到你下筆了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個剛畢業、剛離職、剛分手，站在人生空白頁前慌張的朋友——告訴他空白是開始，不是結束
variations: 更短：人生不是一本有結局的書，是一本要自己寫的筆記本；空白頁是換你下筆了
鼓勵版：別怕那頁是空的，怕的應該是你以為它已經寫完了

en.content:
A K-drama line
for anyone standing in front of a blank stretch of life,
feeling stuck:

"I used to think life was a book —
you hit the last page and it's over.
Then I realized
it's actually a notebook,
and every page is one I have to fill in myself.

So when I reach a blank page,
it isn't the ending.
It's the part I haven't written yet."

The blankness you're in right now
isn't an absence of story.
It's your turn to pick up the pen.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who just graduated, just quit, or just broke up, frozen in front of a blank page of life — tell them blank means beginning, not ending
variations: Shorter: life isn't a book with an ending. It's a notebook you fill in yourself. The blank page is just your turn to write.
Encouraging version: don't be scared the page is empty. Be scared only if you thought it was already finished.

items.sourceNote: 미지의 서울奶奶安慰自責的孫女，躲避不是膽小是為了活下去，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇裡有一段奶奶的話，
專門講給那些一直罵自己「沒用」的人聽：

「鹿為了躲獅子而逃跑，
你會說牠是廢物嗎？
寄居蟹怕被吃掉而躲進殼裡，
你會說牠是膽小鬼嗎？

牠們都只是想活下去而已。
你躲起來，
也只是想活下去而已。」

你以為的逃避，
很多時候，
只是你拼了命想保護自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個一直怪自己「太弱、太會逃」的朋友——告訴他，想活下去從來不是罪
variations: 更短：鹿躲獅子不叫廢物，你保護自己也不叫逃避；那叫想活下去
溫柔版：你不是太膽小，你只是太想好好活著——這沒有錯

en.content:
There's a grandmother's line in a K-drama,
meant for everyone who keeps calling themselves useless:

"When a deer runs from a lion,
do you call it trash?
When a hermit crab hides in its shell
so it won't get eaten,
do you call it a coward?

They're just trying to stay alive.
You hid
because you were trying to stay alive too."

What you keep calling running away
is, so often,
just you fighting hard to protect yourself.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who keeps blaming themselves for being 'too weak' or 'always running' — tell them wanting to survive was never a crime
variations: Shorter: a deer fleeing a lion isn't trash. You protecting yourself isn't running away. It's wanting to live.
Gentle version: you're not too much of a coward. You just wanted, badly, to stay alive — and there's nothing wrong with that.

items.sourceNote: Our Unwritten Seoul慢的一方善於等待，把等待說成一種能力，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇裡有一句很安靜的告白：

「他們說，
愛得比較多的那一個，
注定要等。

沒關係，
等待這件事，
我剛好很擅長。」

聽起來很委屈，
其實很有底氣。

願意等的人，
跟卑微無關，
是太確定——
確定這個人，
值得他把時間花成這個樣子。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個正在默默等一個人、又怕自己看起來太卑微的朋友——告訴他，等待不是輸，是確定
variations: 更短：愛得多的人要等，沒關係，我剛好很擅長等
告白版：我不是在勉強自己等你，我是太確定你值得，才願意把時間花成這樣

en.content:
There's a very quiet confession in a K-drama:

"They say
the one who loves more
is the one who has to wait.

That's fine.
Waiting
just happens to be something I'm good at."

It sounds like a complaint.
It's actually all confidence.

The person willing to wait
isn't being small.
They're just that certain —
certain this person
is worth spending their time this way.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend quietly waiting for someone, afraid it makes them look pathetic — tell them waiting isn't losing, it's being sure
variations: Shorter: the one who loves more has to wait. That's fine — waiting is something I happen to be good at.
Confession version: I'm not forcing myself to wait for you. I'm just so sure you're worth it that I'll spend my time this way.

items.sourceNote: The Practical Guide To Love關於每個人都是一個宇宙的台詞，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇裡有一句關於相遇的話，
意外地溫柔：

「我去過好多場失敗的約會，
然後才發現一件事──
世界真的好大，
每個人都好不一樣。

我遇過的人，
沒有一個是相似的，
每一個都是一個
獨一無二的宇宙。」

所以你還沒遇到對的人，
跟你夠不夠好無關，
是那個宇宙，
還在來的路上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給連續幾次約會失望、開始懷疑自己的朋友——每一次不對，都是在幫你縮小宇宙的範圍
variations: 更短：每個人都是一個宇宙，你只是還沒遇到對的那一個
安慰版：不是你不夠好，是那個對的宇宙，還在來的路上

en.content:
A K-drama line about meeting people
is unexpectedly gentle:

"I went on so many failed dates,
and then I realized something —
the world is really big,
and everyone is so different.

None of the people I met
were even slightly alike.
Every one of them
was a universe of their own."

So if you haven't met the right one yet,
it isn't that you're not good enough.
That universe
is just still on its way.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend coming off a string of disappointing dates and starting to doubt themselves — every wrong one is narrowing down the universe for you
variations: Shorter: everyone is a universe of their own. You just haven't met the right one yet.
Comfort version: it's not that you're not good enough — the right universe is just still on its way.

items.sourceNote: Dynamite Kiss關於想聽對方嘮叨一輩子的台詞，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
他站在門口，鞋子還沒脫好。

「我回來，
是想聽你唸我。

唸我鞋子亂放、
唸我吃太鹹、
唸我又熬夜。

唸到我七老八十都可以。」

她什麼都沒回，
只是彎下腰，
把他那雙鞋
擺正了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個被另一半嫌東嫌西、其實心裡偷偷甜的人——被念是一種很長很長的喜歡
variations: 更短：我不是想聽你說愛我，我是想聽你念我一輩子
告白版：你那些碎念，我想聽到老，一句都別少

en.content:
The least romantic
yet most romantic confession in a K-drama:

"I came back here
not to hear you say how much you love me.

I came to hear you nag.
Complain that I leave my shoes everywhere,
scold me for eating too salty,
yell at me for staying up late again.

I want to hear you nag at me like that
for the rest of my life."

Really wanting to live with someone
isn't wanting their romance.
It's wanting their nagging.
en.editorNote: Send to the person whose partner is always nitpicking them — but who secretly loves it; being nagged is a very, very long kind of love
variations: Shorter: I don't want to hear you say you love me. I want to hear you nag me for the rest of my life.
Confession version: all that nagging of yours — I want to hear it until we're old, not one word less.

items.sourceNote: Doom at Your Service關於不必一直堅強的台詞，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
孤單的時候，就孤單吧。
難過的時候，就難過吧。

你不用在每一則訊息後面
都補一個笑臉，
也不用每次被問「還好嗎」，
都反射性地回一句「還好」。

沒有人規定你
要在所有人面前
都站得那麼直。

真正把人耗乾的，
往往是那層裝沒事的殼，
痛本身反而還撐得住。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個總是說「我沒事」、其實很久沒好好哭一場的朋友——准你今天不堅強
variations: 更短：你不用每一次都假裝沒事，難過的時候，就好好難過
安慰版：在我面前你可以不堅強，不用裝，我看得出來

en.content:
There's a K-drama line
that seems like nothing while you watch it,
then hits you on the walk home
and your eyes sting:

"When you're lonely, be lonely.
When it's hard, let it be hard.
Don't pretend you're fine every single time.

You don't have to be that strong
in front of everyone."

Turns out the exhausting part
isn't the sadness itself —
it's having to fake being okay
while you're sad.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who always says 'I'm fine' but hasn't let themselves cry in a long time — you're allowed to not be strong today
variations: Shorter: You don't have to fake being okay every time. When it's hard, let it be hard.
Comfort version: You don't have to be strong in front of me. Don't pretend — I can tell.

items.sourceNote: Why Her關於壞事過後總有好事的台詞，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
低潮的時候，你會覺得
全世界都在跟你作對：
壞消息一個接一個，
好像沒有一件事順過。

韓劇裡有句話我一直記得：
「再等一下下，
然後抬頭看看周圍。
你會發現好事正在發生，
而且你身邊
一直都有好人。」

壞事不是停不下來，
只是好事比較安靜，
要你願意停下來，
才看得見。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個最近諸事不順、覺得自己被全世界針對的朋友——好事其實一直在，只是比較安靜
variations: 更短：壞事很吵，好事很安靜，你要停下來才聽得見
鼓勵版：再撐一下下，抬頭看看，好人一直都在你身邊

en.content:
When you're down, it feels like
the whole world is against you:
bad news, one after another,
like nothing will ever go right.

There's a K-drama line I keep:
"Wait just a little longer,
then look around you.
You'll see good things happening,
and good people
have been there all along."

Bad things aren't unstoppable.
Good things are just quieter —
you have to stop
to actually see them.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who's been having a rough stretch and feels singled out by the universe — the good stuff is there, it's just quieter
variations: Shorter: Bad things are loud, good things are quiet. You have to stop to hear them.
Encouragement version: Hang on a little longer, look up — the good people have been beside you the whole time.

items.sourceNote: The Good Bad Mother關於你不是壞掉只是在復原的台詞，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
你以為自己壞掉了。
沒辦法像以前一樣開心，
做什麼都提不起勁，
連假裝都覺得累。

但韓劇裡那句話是這樣說的：
「你不是壞掉了，
你只是在復原。」

復原本來就慢，
本來就會反覆，
本來就會有幾天
感覺像退回原點。

那不是你不夠好，
那是你正在好起來的證據。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個正在低谷、覺得自己「是不是壞掉了」的人——你沒壞，你只是在復原的路上
variations: 更短：你不是壞掉了，你只是在復原，慢一點沒關係
自我對話版：今天又退回原點也沒關係，復原本來就會反覆

en.content:
You think you're broken.
Can't feel happy like before,
no energy for anything,
even pretending feels exhausting.

But the K-drama line goes:
"You're not broken.
You're healing."

Healing is slow by nature,
it loops back by nature,
there will be days
that feel like square one.

That's not you failing.
That's proof you're getting better.
en.editorNote: Send to someone in a low place wondering if they're 'broken' — you're not, you're just on the way back
variations: Shorter: You're not broken. You're healing. Slow is okay.
Self-talk version: Back to square one again today? That's fine. Healing loops by nature.

items.sourceNote: Lovely Runner關於想把青春最亮的瞬間留給你的台詞，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇裡最讓人心臟漏一拍的告白，
不是「我愛你」，
是這一句：

「我不知道自己會活到什麼時候，
但如果我的青春裡
有一個最閃亮的瞬間，
我希望那個瞬間，
是跟你一起的。」

喜歡一個人到極致，
不是想要你的未來，
是願意把自己
最好的那一刻，
留給你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個讓你覺得「最好的時光都想跟他一起過」的人——這是最高級的告白
variations: 更短：如果我的青春有一個最亮的瞬間，我想那是和你一起的
深情版：我最好的那一刻，不想自己擁有，想留給你

en.content:
The most heart-skipping confession
in a K-drama isn't "I love you."
It's this:

"I don't know how long I'll live,
but if there's one brightest moment
in my whole youth,
I want that moment
to be with you."

Liking someone to the absolute limit
isn't wanting their future —
it's being willing to give them
the best moment
you'll ever have.
en.editorNote: Send to the person who makes you feel like you want to spend your best times with them — this is the highest-tier confession
variations: Shorter: If my youth has one brightest moment, I want it to be with you.
Tender version: My best moment — I don't want to keep it for myself. I want to give it to you.

items.sourceNote: 韓劇關於每個人都有自己花期的台詞，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
看著別人一個個往前跑——
升職的、結婚的、買房的，
只有你還停在原地，
覺得自己是不是慢了、廢了、落後了。

韓劇裡有句話想送給你：
「你是一朵秋天才開的花。
現在還是春天，
別急。
等到秋天，
你會開得很漂亮。」

你不是開不出來，
你只是花期還沒到。
別人的春天，
不是你的時間表。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個一直在跟同齡人比較、覺得自己落後的朋友——你只是花期還沒到，不是開不出來
variations: 更短：你不是落後，你只是花期還沒到，別人的春天不是你的時間表
鼓勵版：有的人春天開，有的人秋天開，你會開的，等一下就好

en.content:
Watching everyone else sprint ahead —
promotions, weddings, mortgages —
while you're still standing in place,
wondering if you're slow, useless, falling behind.

There's a K-drama line for you:
"You're a flower that blooms in autumn.
It's still spring.
Don't rush.
Wait for fall,
and you'll bloom beautifully."

You're not a flower that can't bloom.
Your season just hasn't come.
Someone else's spring
is not your timeline.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who keeps comparing themselves to their peers and feels behind — your season just hasn't come, that's all
variations: Shorter: You're not behind. Your season just hasn't come. Someone else's spring isn't your timeline.
Encouragement version: Some bloom in spring, some in autumn. You'll bloom — just wait a little.

items.sourceNote: 韓劇人生勵志台詞整理，關於後悔與當下選擇，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
二十五歲那年你說，
等存夠錢就去。

三十五歲那年你打開同一個網頁，
看了看機票，
關掉，
說等下一個連假。

十年之間你一次都沒去成，
而那句「下次」，
你已經說了
數不清多少遍。

失敗只會痛一陣子。

沒去過的那個地方，
會痛很久很久。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個一直在猶豫、把想做的事一直往後延的朋友——提醒他後悔比失敗更痛
variations: 更短：失敗不可怕，可怕的是你明明可以，卻選擇了之後再說
鼓勵版：與其以後後悔當初沒做，不如現在就去，做了至少不會問自己『如果當初』

en.content:
There's a K-drama line
that made me stare at the ceiling for a while:

"Don't do anything
you'll regret later.
Because regret
is the cruelest hell in this world."

All those "next time,"
"once I'm ready,"
"now's not the right moment" —

most of them never get a next time.

What hurts isn't the failure.
It's knowing you could have,
and you didn't.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who keeps hesitating and postponing the things they want to do — regret hurts more than failure
variations: Shorter: Failure isn't the scary part. The scary part is that you could have, and you chose 'later.'
Encouragement version: Better to go now than to regret not trying. At least then you'll never have to ask yourself 'what if.'

items.sourceNote: 韓劇愛情金句特輯，關於幸福與值得追求的事物，海岸村恰恰恰主題，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
我們從小被教的是：
好好讀書、找份穩定工作、
存錢、買房、往上爬。

但韓劇裡有人說：
「這世界上，
除了錢和成就，
還有很多值得你去追的東西——
幸福、把自己活成想要的樣子、
世界和平，
還有，愛。」

你不是只能拼命賺。
那些不能放進銀行的東西，
常常才是讓你睡得著的原因。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個把人生過成業績表、忘記為什麼而努力的朋友——提醒他幸福不在存摺裡
variations: 更短：除了錢和成就，幸福、愛、把自己活成想要的樣子，一樣值得你去追
提醒版：有些東西不能存進銀行，但那常常才是讓你晚上睡得著的原因

en.content:
We were raised on the same script:
study hard, get a stable job,
save, buy a house, climb.

But someone in a K-drama said:
"In this world,
besides money and achievement,
there are so many things worth chasing —
happiness, self-fulfillment,
world peace,
and love."

Grinding isn't your only option.
The things you can't put in a bank
are often the reason you can actually sleep.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who's turned life into a performance report and forgotten why they're working so hard — happiness isn't in the bank balance
variations: Shorter: Besides money and achievement — happiness, love, becoming who you want to be — all worth chasing too.
Reminder version: Some things can't go in a bank. But those are usually the ones that let you sleep at night.

items.sourceNote: 韓劇《因為這是我第一次的人生》台詞，關於心動不是搶來的，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
你以為喜歡一個人，
是要主動、要追、要用力抓住——

但韓劇裡有句話戳得很準：
「心，
不是搶得來、也不是抓得住的東西。
它只是，
自己走向你。」

你越用力想留住誰，
他越像握在手裡的沙。

會留下來的人，
不是你拼命抓住的，
是那個願意自己朝你走過來的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個在一段關係裡一直很用力、卻覺得越抓越遠的朋友——心動不是搶來的
variations: 更短：心不是搶來的，也不是抓得住的，它只會自己走向對的人
安慰版：你抓不住的那個人，本來就不是要留下的，會留的人會自己走來

en.content:
You thought liking someone
meant chasing, grabbing, holding on hard —

but a K-drama line nails it:
"A heart
isn't something you snatch or grab.
It simply
comes to you."

The harder you try to keep someone,
the more they slip like sand through your fingers.

The ones who stay
aren't the ones you clung to.
They're the ones who chose
to walk toward you on their own.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who keeps trying so hard in a relationship but feels the other person slipping further away — a heart can't be grabbed
variations: Shorter: A heart can't be snatched or held. It only walks toward the right person on its own.
Comfort version: The one you couldn't hold on to was never meant to stay. The right one comes to you.

items.sourceNote: Beauty321韓劇表白台詞整理，關於兩個人在一起才完整了世界，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇裡最殺的告白，
從來不是「我愛你」三個字。

而是那句：
「不是你讓我的世界變完整，
是因為有你在，
這個世界才終於開始算數。」

意思是——
在遇到你之前，
我也吃飯、也睡覺、也上班，
但那些都只是「在過日子」。

直到你出現，
那些重複的日常，
才第一次有了，
值得記住的理由。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個讓你覺得「平凡的一天突然有意義」的人——有些感受，借韓劇的嘴說出來剛剛好
variations: 更短：遇到你之前我只是活著，遇到你之後我才開始，真正想記住每一天
低調版：我沒有變成更好的人，只是有了你之後，連最普通的日子都捨不得隨便過

en.content:
The deadliest confession in K-dramas
was never the words "I love you."

It's the line:
"It's not that you completed my world —
it's that because you're here,
the world finally started to count."

Meaning —
before I met you,
I ate, I slept, I went to work,
but all of it was just "getting through days."

Until you showed up,
and those repeating ordinary days
finally had,
for the first time, a reason worth remembering.
en.editorNote: Send to the person who made an ordinary day suddenly feel like it mattered — some feelings land best borrowed from a K-drama
variations: Shorter: Before you I was just alive. After you I actually started wanting to remember every day.
Understated version: I didn't become a better person. I just stopped wanting to waste even the most ordinary days, now that you're in them.

items.sourceNote: Because This Is My First Life台詞，關於話也要進到心裡才活得下去，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
她每次都在他房門外
放一碗湯。

隔天早上收回來，
碗還是滿的，
只是涼了。

她說過的每一句
「我這樣是為你好」，
大概也是這樣——

端到門口，
擺著，
涼掉，
再原封不動
端回自己手上。

話這種東西，
要進得去，
才活得下來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個總覺得「我都講這麼清楚了，他怎麼還聽不懂」的朋友——問題可能不在話，在那扇門
variations: 更短：話要進得了心才算數，對著關起來的門再大聲，也只是自己累
提醒版：不是每句真心話都該說出口，先確認對方願意接，那句話才不會白白死掉

en.content:
A K-drama once said something
that sounds soft but lands heavy:

"Words, too, have to get
into a person's heart
before they can keep living."

Meaning —
you can say "it's for your own good" a hundred times,
but if the other person doesn't catch it,
that sentence just
dies in the air.

So sometimes it's not that you didn't say enough.
It's that you've been
shouting at a door
that closed a long time ago.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who keeps thinking 'I explained it so clearly, why don't they get it' — the problem might not be the words, but the door
variations: Shorter: Words only count if they reach the heart. Yelling at a closed door just tires you out.
Reminder version: Not every honest thing needs to be said out loud. Check that they're willing to catch it first, so the words don't die for nothing.

items.sourceNote: Tatler韓劇寫實金句整理，關於沒有任何一段愛是沒有意義的，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
分手後你最常問自己的，
大概是那句：
「那這一切，到底有什麼意義？」

韓劇替你回答了：
「世界上沒有任何一段愛，
是沒有意義的。
每一次喜歡上一個人，
本身就已經是一種祝福。」

就算最後沒在一起，
你也曾經因為一個人，
變得更勇敢、更柔軟、
更懂得怎麼好好愛——

那不是白費，
那是你帶得走的東西。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個剛分手、一直覺得「那段感情全是浪費」的朋友——有些東西不會因為結束就消失
variations: 更短：沒在一起不代表沒意義，你曾經為一個人變得更好，那部分永遠是你的
療癒版：那段感情沒有白費，它教會你的事，會在下一個對的人面前，悄悄派上用場

en.content:
After a breakup, the question
you ask yourself most
is probably: "So what was the point of all of it?"

A K-drama answers for you:
"There isn't any love in this world
that's meaningless.
Falling for someone
is, in itself, already a blessing."

Even if you didn't end up together,
you once became braver, softer,
better at loving well —
because of one person.

That wasn't wasted.
That's the part you get to keep.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend fresh off a breakup who keeps thinking 'that whole relationship was a waste' — some things don't disappear just because it ended
variations: Shorter: Not ending up together doesn't mean it was meaningless. You became better for someone once, and that part is yours forever.
Healing version: That relationship wasn't a waste. What it taught you will quietly come in handy in front of the next right person.

items.sourceNote: 韓劇愛情台詞整理，關於愛情的不是大小而是溫度，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
有人問：「每個人最後
都是跟最愛的人在一起嗎？」

韓劇給了一個很成熟的答案：
「不是的。
喜歡的大小其實都差不多，
差別在於溫度。」

有些人讓你燒得很燙，
燙到你變得不像自己；
而對的那個人，
是那種剛剛好的溫度——
讓你還能好好做自己。

所以別只看誰讓你最心動，
要看誰在的時候，
你最像你自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個在「最愛的」跟「最適合的」之間猶豫的朋友——提醒他溫度比火花更重要
variations: 更短：愛得最轟烈的不一定是對的，對的人是讓你還能好好做自己的那種剛好溫度
犀利版：能讓你燒起來的人很多，能讓你燒得剛剛好、不把自己燒沒的人很少

en.content:
Someone asks:
"Does everyone end up
with the person they loved most?"

A K-drama gives a grown-up answer:
"No. The size of the love
wasn't really different.
It was the temperature."

Some people burn you so hot
you stop recognizing yourself;
the right one
is the temperature that's just right —
the one who lets you stay you.

So don't only ask who makes your heart race.
Ask who you're most yourself around.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend torn between 'the one I loved most' and 'the one who fits' — remind them temperature beats sparks
variations: Shorter: The most intense love isn't always the right one. The right person is the temperature that lets you stay yourself.
Sharper: Plenty of people can set you on fire. Few can keep you at the temperature where you don't burn yourself away.

items.sourceNote: 韓劇台詞整理，關於愛得多的人負責等待，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
「你知道嗎，
通常都是愛得比較多的那個人，
負責等。」

「而我，剛好很會等。」

這句話聽起來很灑脫，
但只有等過的人才懂——
所謂「很會等」，
不是不在乎，
是太在乎，
所以把急著想靠近的力氣，
全部轉成了耐心。

會等的人不是不痛，
是寧願自己痛一點，
也想等到那個人準備好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個正在默默等一個人的朋友——讓他知道他的等待不是傻，是溫柔
variations: 更短：愛得多的那個人負責等，而會等不代表不痛，是寧願自己痛也想等對方準備好
心疼版：別再說自己很會等了，那不是天賦，是你把所有想衝過去的衝動，硬生生忍成了耐心

en.content:
"You know, the one who loves more
is usually the one who waits."

"And me — I happen to be good at waiting."

It sounds so easy-going,
but only someone who's waited gets it:
"good at waiting"
doesn't mean not caring.
It means caring so much
you turned every urge to rush closer
into patience instead.

The one who waits isn't in less pain.
They'd just rather hurt a little themselves
than rush someone who isn't ready.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend quietly waiting on someone — let them know their patience isn't foolish, it's tenderness
variations: Shorter: The one who loves more does the waiting. And being good at waiting doesn't mean it hurts less — it means you'd rather hurt than rush them.
Tender version: Stop calling yourself good at waiting. That's not a talent — it's you forcing every urge to run toward them into patience.

items.sourceNote: Cosmo韓劇勵志台詞整理，關於不必完美也值得被愛，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
你是不是也常覺得，
「等我變得更好、更完整，
才有資格被好好愛？」

有句韓劇台詞戳破了這個想法：
「你不需要先變得完美，
才值得被愛。」

愛不是給滿分的人的獎品，
它不是你考到一百分才能領的東西。
你身上那些覺得不夠好的地方，
那些缺角、那些笨拙，
也都在被愛的範圍裡。

別等到完美才肯讓人靠近——
你現在這樣，就已經值得了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個總覺得「要先變更好才配被愛」而把人推遠的朋友——他現在這樣就已經夠了
variations: 更短：愛不是考一百分才能領的獎品，你那些覺得不夠好的地方，也在被愛的範圍裡
溫柔版：別等到完美才肯讓人靠近，你現在這樣——有缺角、會笨拙——就已經值得被好好愛

en.content:
Do you also keep thinking,
"Once I'm better, more put-together,
then I'll deserve to be loved properly"?

A K-drama line cuts right through that:
"You don't need to be perfect
to be worthy of love."

Love isn't a prize for the flawless.
It's not something you collect
only after scoring a hundred percent.
The parts of you that feel not-enough,
the chipped edges, the clumsiness —
those are inside the range of being loved too.

Don't wait until you're perfect to let someone close.
The way you are right now is already enough.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who keeps people at arm's length thinking 'I have to get better before I deserve love' — they're already enough as they are
variations: Shorter: Love isn't a prize you collect after scoring a hundred percent. The parts of you that feel not-enough are inside the range of being loved too.
Gentle version: Don't wait until you're perfect to let someone close. The way you are now — chipped edges, clumsiness and all — is already worth loving.

items.sourceNote: 韓劇《這份愛戀，可以翻譯嗎》告白台詞整理，關於理智撐到最後還是淪陷，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
他把咖啡端過來，
手看起來很穩。

放下的時候，
杯緣還是磕到了桌角，
發出很小的一聲。

他愣了一秒，
然後說：

「我本來想撐住理智
撐到最後再講。

結果我先瘋了。
我最近一直看到極光，
其實已經有一陣子了。」

三秒鐘而已，
她卻清楚地聽見，
有個人在她面前
整個塌下來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個明明喜歡得要命卻一直假裝冷靜的朋友——告訴他藏不住的時候，反而最動人
variations: 更短：最浪漫的告白不是「我愛你」，而是「我本來想撐住理智，結果先瘋的是我」
告白版：我本來想忍到最後，結果一看到你，理智就先投降了——這就是我的告白

en.content:
The most romantic confession
often isn't the words "I love you,"
it's someone trying so hard to stay composed
and losing to their own heart anyway.

A K-drama confesses like this:
"Out of the two of us,
I meant to keep my sanity till the very end —
but I'm the one who went mad first.
I keep seeing auroras.
Have for a while now, actually.
This is me confessing."

More than a flawless line,
it's that 'I can't hide it anymore' unraveling
that makes a heart skip a beat.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who's crazy about someone but keeps playing it cool — tell them the moment they stop hiding it is the most disarming part
variations: Shorter: The most romantic confession isn't 'I love you' — it's 'I meant to keep my sanity till the end, but I'm the one who went mad first.'
Confession version: I meant to hold out till the end, but one look at you and my sanity surrendered first — and that's my confession.

items.sourceNote: 韓劇《今生也請多指教》15句人生寶藏台詞，關於放開心愛之人的手，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
有一部韓劇講一個活過好幾世的人，
他說過一句話，看完很久都散不掉：

「就算我活了那麼多次，
有一個瞬間我始終學不會習慣——
就是不得不放開最喜歡的人的手的那一刻。」

原來有些事不會因為經歷很多次
就變得比較不痛。
它每一次都一樣痛，
只是你假裝自己已經習慣了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個剛經歷離別、卻一直說「我沒事，我習慣了」的朋友——讓他知道不習慣也沒關係
variations: 更短：有些事不會因為發生很多次就比較不痛，它每次都一樣痛，你只是學會了裝沒事
告別版：我練習了很多次說再見，但放開你手的那一刻，我發現我一次都沒真正學會

en.content:
There's a K-drama about someone who's lived many lifetimes.
He says one thing that won't leave you for days:

"Even after living so many times,
there's one moment I never learned to get used to —
the moment I have to let go of the hand
of the person I love most."

Turns out some things don't hurt less
just because you've done them a hundred times.
They hurt exactly the same each time.
You only pretend you've gotten used to it.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who just went through a breakup but keeps saying 'I'm fine, I'm used to it' — let them know it's okay not to be used to it
variations: Shorter: Some things don't hurt less for happening often. They hurt the same every time — you just learned to fake being fine.
Goodbye version: I practiced saying goodbye so many times, but the moment I let go of your hand, I realized I'd never actually learned how.

items.sourceNote: 韓劇《好搭檔》離婚律師金句40選，關於婚姻與信任的現實，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
有一部韓劇的女主角是離婚律師，
她看過太多感情爛掉的現場，
講過一句很冷但很準的話：

「會出問題的感情，
其實早就有徵兆了。
只是當事人選擇相信
『他只是最近比較累』，
相信了一年又一年。」

感情很少是突然死掉的，
它通常是慢慢地、
在你一次又一次說服自己「應該沒事吧」之中
安靜地走的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個一直幫對方找藉口、說「他只是最近比較忙」的朋友——讓他誠實面對自己看到的徵兆
variations: 更短：感情很少是突然死的，它是在你一次次說「應該沒事吧」之中慢慢走掉的
提醒版：你不是不知道哪裡怪怪的，你只是太想相信沒事——這兩件事差很多

en.content:
There's a K-drama where the lead is a divorce lawyer.
She's seen too many relationships rot up close,
and she drops a line that's cold but exact:

"Relationships that fall apart
almost always showed signs early on.
The person just chose to believe
'he's only been tired lately' —
and believed it for year after year."

Love rarely dies suddenly.
It usually goes slowly, quietly,
in all the times you talked yourself into
'it's probably nothing.'
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who keeps making excuses for their partner — 'he's just been busy lately' — and help them be honest about the signs they've seen
variations: Shorter: Love rarely dies suddenly. It dies slowly, in every time you told yourself 'it's probably nothing.'
Reminder version: You're not unaware something's off. You just badly want it to be nothing — and those two are very different things.

items.sourceNote: TVBS玩美研究室最撩人韓劇愛情語錄整理，告白心動場景，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
他從來沒說過喜歡你。

他只說：
「你什麼都不用為我做，
你在那裡就好，
讓我每天有一個
想回去的地方。」

聽起來像在拜託你幫個小忙。

其實他把整顆心，
連同那把鑰匙，
一起放到你手上了。

一個人願意把「回家」這兩個字
指定給你——

你覺得那還能算普通的關心嗎？
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個喜歡含蓄表達、不會直接說「我愛你」的朋友——告訴他這種藏起來的告白其實最動人
variations: 更短：你不用為我做什麼，你只要在那裡，讓我每天有一個想回去的地方就好
土味版：別人回家是回到一個地方，我回家是回到你——你就是我的地址

en.content:
What K-dramas do best
isn't saying "I like you" —
it's hiding the liking inside a line
that sounds like it's about something else entirely:

"You don't have to do anything for me.
Just be there,
so I have a place I want to come back to every day."

On the surface he asks for nothing.
In reality he's just handed you
his entire heart —
and that's the most dangerous kind of confession,
because you think you're merely needed,
not realizing you've already become someone's everything.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who expresses things indirectly and never just says 'I love you' — tell them the hidden kind of confession is often the most moving
variations: Shorter: You don't have to do anything for me. Just be there, so I have a place I want to come home to every day.
Cheesy version: Other people go home to a place. I go home to you — you're my address.

items.sourceNote: Tatler Asia比「我愛你」更動聽的韓劇台詞整理，含蓄表白場景，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇教會你一件事：
比「我愛你」更難招架的，
是「我想見你」。

「就算只是想見你一面，
我也願意走到這裡。
只要能見到你，
我什麼都可以做。」

「我愛你」是一種狀態，
「我願意為了見你走這麼遠」
是一個行動——
而人，永遠敗給行動。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個嘴上不會說愛、但會默默開兩小時車去見你的人——讓他知道你都看在眼裡
variations: 更短：就算只是見你一面，我也願意走這麼遠——能見到你，我什麼都做得到
現實版：他沒說過一次愛我，但每次我隨口說想吃什麼，他隔天就出現在我家樓下

en.content:
K-dramas teach you one thing:
harder to resist than "I love you"
is "I wanted to see you."

"Even if it's just to see you once,
I'd come all this way.
As long as I get to see you,
there's nothing I wouldn't do."

"I love you" is a state.
"I'd travel this far just to see you"
is an action —
and people always lose to action.
en.editorNote: Send to the person who never says the words but quietly drives two hours just to see you — let them know you noticed
variations: Shorter: Even just to see you once, I'd come this far. As long as I get to see you, there's nothing I wouldn't do.
Real-life version: He's never once said he loves me, but every time I mention I'm craving something, he shows up outside my place the next day.

items.sourceNote: Popbee低潮時的韓劇人生台詞整理，《我的出走日記》療癒系語錄，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
我要的其實很簡單，
但也很難。

我要你從早上睜開眼，
到晚上闔上眼，
都覺得有我在真好。

滿滿的那種。

你被填滿了，
我也就跟著被填滿了。

聽起來很狂吧。

可是勉強的喜歡我收過太多次，
那種東西放三天就壞。

我寧願要一種
連你自己都戒不掉的
「有你真好」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個在感情裡總是委屈求全的朋友——提醒他，值得的關係不是互相忍耐，是互相覺得「有你真好」
variations: 更短：我不要你勉強愛我，我要你打從心底覺得，有我真好
現實版：愛情會累，但那種一想到對方就覺得「還好有你」的感覺，不會

en.content:
The most piercing line in My Liberation Notes
isn't about love.
It's this:

"I don't need you to love me.
I need you to — worship me.
From the moment you open your eyes
till you fall asleep,
fully, completely.
You get filled up,
and so do I."

It sounds intense on the surface.
What she's really saying is:
I don't want your reluctant affection.
I want the kind
where someone genuinely feels
"I'm glad you exist" —
and that's far harder than love.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who always settles and shrinks themselves in relationships — remind them a worthwhile bond isn't mutual tolerance, it's both people feeling glad the other exists
variations: Shorter: I don't want you to force yourself to love me. I want you to genuinely feel glad I exist.
Real-life version: Love gets tired. But that feeling of 'thank god you're here' the moment you think of someone — that doesn't.

items.sourceNote: Beauty321韓劇心動表白台詞整理，「因為我們在一起完整了世界」主題，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇最會的告白句型，
是把對方變成一個世界的單位：

「在遇見你之前，
我的世界是完整的。
遇見你之後我才發現，
原來那時候少了一塊，
只是我自己不知道。」

這句話的可怕之處在於——
它沒有說「我需要你」，
它說的是
「沒有你，我連自己缺了什麼都不知道」。

比起被需要，
被一個人這樣看見，
才是真的逃不掉。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個讓你覺得「原來我以前缺了一塊」的人——有些缺口，是遇見之後才發現的
variations: 更短：遇見你之前我以為自己很完整，遇見你之後才知道，原來少了一塊
土味版：別人說你是我的另一半，我說你是我本來就缺、但一直沒發現的那一塊

en.content:
The K-drama confession formula that works
turns the other person into a unit of measure
for an entire world:

"Before I met you,
my world felt complete.
It was only after
that I realized a piece had been missing
all along —
I just didn't know it."

The terrifying part of that line:
it doesn't say "I need you."
It says
"without you, I didn't even know
what I was missing."

Being needed is one thing.
Being seen like that
is the part you can't escape.
en.editorNote: Send to the person who made you realize 'a piece of me was missing all along' — some gaps you only notice after you've met someone
variations: Shorter: Before you, I thought I was whole. After you, I realized a piece had been missing the whole time.
Cheesy version: People say you're my other half. I say you're the piece I was always missing and never noticed.

items.sourceNote: WEPEOPLE《苦盡柑來遇見你》金句整理，「不要退而求其次」人生主題，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇最戳人的人生金句，
往往不是教你怎麼贏，
是提醒你別太早認輸。

「不要退而求其次。
你會說『差不多就好』，
通常不是因為你真的滿足，
是因為你太累了，
累到忘記自己本來想要什麼。」

退而求其次不是壞事，
壞的是——
你連自己退了多遠，
都不記得了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個總說「這樣就好」、但眼神裡明明還有想要的東西的朋友——累可以休息，但別把累當成答案
variations: 更短：『差不多就好』這句話，要小心——它有時候是知足，有時候是放棄，差別只在你還記不記得本來要什麼
現實版：人不是被夢想打敗的，是被『反正也來不及了』這句話慢慢勸退的

en.content:
The K-drama life lines that hit hardest
usually don't teach you how to win —
they just stop you from giving up too early.

"Don't settle for second best.
When you say 'this is good enough,'
it's often not because you're satisfied —
it's because you're exhausted.
So tired you forgot
what you actually wanted."

Settling isn't the problem.
The problem is
when you can't even remember
how far you've drifted from the original.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who keeps saying 'this is fine' while their eyes say otherwise — being tired is allowed, but don't mistake tired for the answer
variations: Shorter: 'Good enough' is a tricky phrase. Sometimes it's contentment, sometimes it's surrender — and the only difference is whether you still remember what you were after.
Real talk: People aren't defeated by their dreams. They're slowly talked out of them by the phrase 'it's too late anyway.'

items.sourceNote: KORB 80句韓劇愛情台詞，「遇見你之後每天都漫長」時間感主題，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇有一種告白，
是用時間來計算的。

「我一個人活了很多年，
那些年加起來，
還沒有遇見你之後的這幾個月長。

不是日子變慢了，
是以前的我，
根本沒在認真活，
只是讓時間流過去而已。」

最動人的不是「我愛你」，
是「遇見你之後，
我才開始把每一天當一天過」。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個讓你開始認真過日子的人——有些人不是讓你心動而已，是讓你終於覺得時間值得被記住
variations: 更短：遇見你之前我活了好幾年，但好像是遇見你之後，我才真的開始活
土味版：別人說一天二十四小時，自從認識你，我覺得不夠用了

en.content:
There's a K-drama confession
measured entirely in time.

"I lived alone for years.
Add all those years up —
they still don't feel as long
as the few months since I met you.

It's not that time slowed down.
It's that the old me
wasn't really living,
just letting the days pass through."

The moving part isn't 'I love you.'
It's 'since I met you,
I finally started living each day
like it was actually a day.'
en.editorNote: Send to the person who made you start living on purpose — some people don't just make your heart race, they make time finally feel worth remembering
variations: Shorter: I lived for years before you. But it feels like I only started actually living after.
Cheesy version: They say a day has twenty-four hours. Since I met you, that somehow isn't enough.

items.sourceNote: POPBEE 低潮時的韓劇台詞，「沒有走不出的隧道」希望主題，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
去年冬天你走進去的時候，
以為那條隧道沒有盡頭，
以為再也看不到光了。

今年冬天你在超商排隊結帳，
突然想起那件事，
想了兩秒，
就又去想晚餐要吃什麼。

痛沒有消失，
它只是變短了。

世界上沒有永遠的愛，
也沒有永遠的痛。

你現在在隧道裡，
不代表你住在這裡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個正卡在某段黑暗裡、覺得永遠出不去的人——不用他馬上好起來，只要他記得這是隧道，不是終點
variations: 更短：你現在在隧道裡，不代表你住在這裡——再走一段，光會自己出現
陪伴版：我不會說『一定會好』，我只說——這段路再長也有盡頭，而且我會陪你走到看見光那一刻

en.content:
The most comforting K-drama line
isn't 'it'll get better.'
It reframes pain as a tunnel:

"Everyone passes through
a stretch of darkness in life,
so long that you start to believe
you'll never see light again.

But there's no tunnel without an exit.
There's no love that lasts forever,
and no pain that lasts forever either."

It doesn't tell you to cheer up.
It just reminds you —
being in the tunnel right now
doesn't mean you live here.
en.editorNote: Send to the person stuck in a dark stretch who feels they'll never get out — they don't have to feel better right away, just remember it's a tunnel, not the destination
variations: Shorter: Being in the tunnel right now doesn't mean you live here. Walk a little further — the light shows up on its own.
Companion version: I won't say 'it'll definitely be fine.' I'll say this — no matter how long this stretch is, it ends, and I'll walk it with you until we see light.

items.sourceNote: 女人我最大《今生也請多指教》台詞，「大家都是裝出來的」成長主題，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇有一句很現實的台詞，
聽完整個人鬆了一口氣：

「人到死那天，
都不會真的變得很懂事。

那些看起來很成熟的大人，
其實也只是裝得比較久，
裝到自己都快相信了而已。」

你以為長大就會自動學會應對一切，
結果只是學會
在不知道怎麼辦的時候，
臉上先撐住。

所以你不是還沒長大，
你只是還沒學會裝——
而那其實沒什麼好急的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個一直覺得『別人都好成熟、只有我還在裝大人』的朋友——其實大家都在裝，你只是比較誠實
variations: 更短：所謂的成熟，常常只是裝得比較久、裝到自己都快信了
安慰版：你不是不夠成熟，你只是還沒學會在慌的時候面不改色——而那一點都不急

en.content:
There's a brutally honest K-drama line
that somehow makes you exhale:

"No one ever really
has it all figured out,
not even on their last day.

The grown-ups who seem so composed
are just better at pretending —
pretending long enough
that they almost believe it."

You assumed growing up meant
automatically knowing how to handle everything.
Turns out it just means
learning to keep a straight face
when you have no idea what to do.

So you're not behind.
You just haven't learned to pretend yet —
and honestly, there's no rush.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who thinks 'everyone else has it together and I'm just faking being an adult' — everyone's faking, you're just more honest about it
variations: Shorter: What we call maturity is often just pretending long enough that you start to believe it yourself.
Reassuring version: You're not less mature. You just haven't learned to keep a straight face when you're panicking — and there's no rush to.

items.sourceNote: POPBEE 2026治癒系韓劇台詞「你的幸福為什麼要問別人」，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
有句韓劇台詞看完，
突然不想再問別人的意見了：

「你的幸福，
為什麼要去問別人？

好像非得有人點頭，
你才敢承認自己過得好。」

你習慣先看別人的臉色，
再決定自己能不能開心。

但快樂這件事，
從來不需要外面的認證——
你說你過得好，那就算數。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個總在等別人認可、才敢覺得自己過得不錯的朋友
variations: 更短：你的快樂不需要別人蓋章，你說了算
提醒版：別再拿別人的標準衡量自己的幸福，幸不幸福只有你自己知道

en.content:
A K-drama line that made me stop
asking everyone else for permission:

"Your happiness —
why do you keep asking other people about it?

As if you need someone to nod first
before you're allowed to admit
you're actually doing okay."

You check everyone's face
before deciding whether you get to feel good.

But happiness was never something
that needed outside approval —
if you say you're doing well, that counts.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who waits for everyone's approval before letting themselves feel fine
variations: Shorter: Your happiness doesn't need anyone's stamp of approval. You decide.
Reminder version: Stop measuring your happiness against other people's standards — only you know if you're okay.

items.sourceNote: KORB《Dynamite Kiss》台詞「想聽你唸我一輩子」，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
我認真算過。

在一起的這七年，
你唸我亂放鞋子大概兩千次，
唸我吃太鹹大概一千次，
唸我又熬夜的次數
我早就數不清了。

甜言蜜語你總共講過三句，
我每一句都記得。

可是真正讓我不想搬走的，
其實是那兩千次。

被你嫌的每一天，
我都睡得很好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個會嫌你、卻一刻都離不開你的另一半——被唸也是一種被愛
variations: 更短：我想聽你唸我一輩子，這就是我想留下來的理由
告白版：我要的不是浪漫的火花，是每天有你在身邊、連被你嫌都安心

en.content:
A K-drama confession
that sounds unromantic but is the most romantic kind:

"I'm here
because I want to hear you nag at me
for the rest of my life."

Other people want sweet nothings.
He wants your grumbling —
the 'you left your stuff everywhere again,'
the 'you stayed up way too late again.'

Because the people who actually mean forever
aren't after the spark of new love.
They want you beside them every day,
so much that even being nagged feels like home.
en.editorNote: Send to the partner who nags you but can't go a moment without you — being nagged is its own kind of being loved
variations: Shorter: I want to hear you nag at me for the rest of my life — that's the whole reason I'm staying.
Confession version: I don't want the spark of new love. I want you beside me every day, so much that even your nagging feels like home.

items.sourceNote: 《Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha》人生沒有標準答案台詞，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
有句韓劇台詞，
講出了我們從小被騙的一件事：

「人生不是數學題，
沒有正確答案，
也沒有標準解法。

它只是丟給你一道題，
剩下的，看你怎麼解。」

我們花了好多年，
以為人生有一條對的路。

後來才發現——
根本沒有對的路，
只有你選了之後，
再想辦法把它走對的路。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個一直在問「我這樣選對不對」的朋友——告訴他沒有對不對，只有走下去之後的負責
variations: 更短：人生不是數學題，沒有標準答案——只有你選了之後再走對的路
迷惘版：別再找正確答案了，根本沒有那種東西——你的選擇本身，就是答案

en.content:
A K-drama line
that undoes something we were told as kids:

"Life isn't a math problem.
There's no correct answer,
no clean solution.

You're just handed the problem,
and the rest is up to you."

We spent years
believing there was one right path.

Turns out
there is no right path —
only the one you pick,
and then spend your life
making right.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend stuck asking 'is this the right choice' — tell them there's no right or wrong, just owning what comes after
variations: Shorter: Life isn't a math problem with one answer — just the path you pick, then make right.
Lost version: Stop hunting for the correct answer, it doesn't exist — your choice itself is the answer.

items.sourceNote: 《Tomorrow》只要活著就有機會台詞，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
有句韓劇台詞，
短短一句，卻接住了很多快撐不住的人：

「只要你還活著，
就還有機會
把它修好。」

我們常常以為
搞砸了就是永遠完了。

但其實沒有那麼絕對——
只要你還在，
那件你以為毀掉的事，
就還留著一個被修好的可能。

結局還沒寫，
因為你還在寫。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個覺得「我把一切都搞砸了」的朋友——只要還在，就還有下一頁
variations: 更短：只要你還活著，再糟的事都還有被修好的可能
撐不住版：別急著下結論，故事還沒結束——因為你還在，就還有機會

en.content:
A K-drama line,
short enough to fit on one breath, that has caught a lot of people:

"As long as you're alive,
you still have a chance
to fix it."

We so easily assume
that messing up means it's over for good.

But it's rarely that final —
as long as you're still here,
the thing you thought you ruined
still holds a chance of being mended.

The ending isn't written,
because you're still writing it.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend convinced they've ruined everything — as long as they're still here, there's a next page
variations: Shorter: As long as you're alive, even the worst of it still has a chance of being fixed.
Barely-holding-on version: Don't call it yet — the story isn't over, because you're still in it.

items.sourceNote: 《When Life Gives You Tangerines》(2025) 愛的溫度而非強度台詞，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
二十歲的時候，
我以為愛情要像仙女棒，
拿在手上會燙，
亮到看不見旁邊的人。

現在我家玄關的抽屜裡，
永遠有一個充飽電的暖暖包。

冬天出門前，
你會把它塞進我口袋，
什麼話都沒說。

它不燙手，
溫度剛剛好，
可以握一整個下午。

會留下來的愛情，
大概都長這樣。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個還在等「轟轟烈烈」的朋友——最好的愛不是燙的，是剛好讓你想一直握著的溫度
variations: 更短：愛重要的不是有多濃烈，是有多溫暖
成熟版：年輕時要的是心跳，後來才懂——能握一輩子的，是剛剛好的溫度

en.content:
A K-drama line
that redefines what good love looks like:

"What matters in love
was never how intense it is,
but how warm."

When we're young
we think love has to be a blaze,
that it only counts if your heart's about to burst.

Later you learn —
the kind of love that actually stays
doesn't scald.
It's the right warmth,
the kind you'd keep holding all winter.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend still waiting for the grand blaze — the best love isn't scalding, it's the warmth you want to keep holding
variations: Shorter: What matters in love was never how intense it is, but how warm.
Grown-up version: Young, you want the racing heart. Later you learn the love that lasts is just the right warmth.

items.sourceNote: 《鬼怪》「無論一千次還是一萬次，我都想再遇見你」概念，原創改編為觀眾視角吐槽

zh-tw.content:
「就算重來一千次、一萬次，
我還是會選擇遇見你。」

聽起來很滿，很命定。

可是這句話真正的重量，
藏在那沒說出口的後半段。

那個人是看完全部才說的——
看過吵到天亮的那一晚，
看過機場那次，
看過你最難看的樣子。

全部看完之後
還敢說要再來一次的人，

你覺得這輩子
能遇到幾個？
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合放在紀念日訊息裡，或傳給一個你「明知會麻煩但還是想選」的人
variations: 短版：重來一萬次我還是選你，不是因為沒看過壞的，是因為看過了還是選你。
反差版：我不會說重來一千次都選你，我頂多說重來這一次，我還是會選你——但這樣就夠了。

en.content:
One kind of confession K-dramas nail:
"Even if I did it over a thousand times,
ten thousand times,
I'd still choose to meet you."

Sounds huge. Sounds fated.

But the part that actually gets you
is the half they don't say out loud:
they're not saying "I have no regrets."
They're saying, "Even knowing it'll hurt this much,
I'd still do it again."

That's not romance.
That's a clear-eyed choice —
having seen all the bad, and still picking you.
en.editorNote: Good for an anniversary text, or for the person you'd knowingly choose again even though it's complicated
variations: Short: I'd choose you ten thousand times over — not because I never saw the bad parts, but because I did and still chose you.
Understated version: I won't say I'd pick you across a thousand lifetimes. I'll just say if I got this one over again, I'd still pick you. That's enough.

items.sourceNote: 2026年話題韓劇「契約結婚」設定觀察（財閥二世×王子），原創吐槽

zh-tw.content:
2026年韓劇又復活了一個老梗：
「契約結婚」。

規則永遠是那三條：
第一，這只是一場交易，別動真感情。
第二，不准愛上對方。
第三，一年後和平分開。

然後你看著螢幕心想：
這三條規則的存在，
唯一的功能就是被打破。

凡是劇裡有人認真訂下「不准愛上你」，
那個人到第八集，
一定愛得比誰都慘。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給一起追契約結婚劇的朋友，配一句「賭第幾集破功」
variations: 短版：韓劇裡只要出現「契約結婚，不准動心」的合約，那份合約就是用來被撕掉的。
延伸版：現實裡的合約是拿來遵守的，韓劇裡的合約是拿來在雨中撕掉、然後告白的。

en.content:
K-dramas revived an old trope in 2026:
the contract marriage.

The rules are always the same three:
One, this is strictly a deal — no real feelings.
Two, do not fall in love with each other.
Three, we split amicably in a year.

And you watch the screen thinking:
the only function of these three rules
is to be broken.

Anyone who solemnly signs
"do not fall in love with me"
is, by episode eight,
falling harder than anyone alive.
en.editorNote: Send to whoever's watching the contract-marriage drama with you, plus 'betting on which episode the rule breaks'
variations: Short: Any K-drama contract that says 'no falling in love' exists purely so it can be torn up later.
Extended: In real life a contract is something you honor. In a K-drama it's something you tear up in the rain right before the confession.

items.sourceNote: 《結束的我們》(Nevertheless)「我愛上了你的混亂」概念，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇裡有一種告白特別真：
「我不是愛上你最好的樣子，
我是愛上你一團亂的樣子。」

這句話為什麼比「你好完美」更打中人？

因為誰都可以喜歡你光鮮的那一面，
那不需要勇氣。

真正稀有的是——
有人看過你崩潰、看過你搞砸、
看過你三天沒回訊息的那種低潮，
然後說：「這樣也沒關係，我還在。」

被人喜歡不難，
被人在最亂的時候還留下來，才難。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個看過你最狼狽卻沒走的人——這比任何情話都重
variations: 短版：喜歡你光鮮的樣子不算什麼，看過你一團亂還留下的人，才是真的。
自省版：我一直想給人看最好的自己，後來才懂——會留下的人，本來就是為了那個亂七八糟的我留下的。

en.content:
There's a confession K-dramas get painfully right:
"I didn't fall for you at your best.
I fell for your mess."

Why does that land harder than "you're perfect"?

Because anyone can like your polished side.
That takes no courage.

What's rare is
someone who's seen you fall apart,
seen you screw up,
seen the low where you ghost everyone for three days —
and says, "That's okay. I'm still here."

Being liked isn't hard.
Being stayed with at your messiest is.
en.editorNote: Send to the person who saw you at your worst and didn't leave — that outweighs any sweet line
variations: Short: Liking you at your best is easy. Staying once they've seen your mess is the real thing.
Reflective: I spent years showing people my best self. Turns out the ones who stay were always staying for the messy version.

items.sourceNote: 韓劇「你活著活著，總會有一刻明白這一切都是為了今天，所以要活下去」概念，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
那年冬天你縮在租來的小房間，
覺得這樣撐著到底有什麼意義。

今年某個很普通的早上，
你在路口等紅燈，
手上拿著剛買的豆漿，
忽然就懂了：

原來那一切，
都是為了走到今天。

意義很少在當下出現。

它會等到很久以後，
等你有一天回頭看，
才發現那些咬著牙撐過去的日子，
剛好拼成了現在的你。

所以，好好活下去。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給正在硬撐、覺得看不到意義的人——意義常常是回頭才看得見的
variations: 短版：撐下去的意義，通常不在當下，而在很久以後你回頭的那一眼。
打氣版：你現在覺得沒意義的每一天，都是未來的你回頭會感謝的那一天。

en.content:
There's a K-drama line that leaves the room quiet:
"As you keep living,
there'll come a moment when you suddenly realize —
all of it
was for today.
So live."

The first time, it sounds a little abstract.

But think of the days you barely got through,
the nights you thought,
"what's even the point of holding on" —

maybe the point isn't in that moment.
Maybe it's on some ordinary morning far from now,
when you look back
and find that everything you survived
quietly assembled into the person you are.
en.editorNote: Send to someone white-knuckling through it and unable to see the point — meaning is usually only visible in hindsight
variations: Short: The point of holding on usually isn't in the moment — it's in the glance back you take much later.
Encouraging: Every day that feels pointless right now is a day future-you will look back on and be grateful you stayed.

items.sourceNote: Dcard追劇板，韓劇「先吃飯了嗎」關心文化觀察，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
這個月我媽傳給我三十一則訊息，
其中二十八則
只有四個字：「吃飯了嗎」。

「我很想你」她一次都沒打過。
「你還好嗎」也沒有。

我算了一下，
二十八次乘以四個字，
一百一十二個字，
講的其實都是同一件事。

想你太重，說不出口。
問你吃飽沒，剛剛好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個嘴上不會說想你、只會問你吃飽沒的家人或朋友——那就是他的告白方式
variations: 短版：「你吃飯了嗎」是東亞人最含蓄的「我想你」。
延伸版：真正在乎你的人，不會問你過得好不好，會直接問你今天吃了什麼——因為他要確認你有好好照顧自己。

en.content:
Watch enough K-dramas and you notice
they all show care the same way:
not "I'm worried about you,"
but "Have you eaten?"

At first it feels overused —
every single show asks it.

Then it clicks:
"Have you eaten?"
is just "I've been thinking about you"
in the form least likely to get rejected.

Saying you miss someone is too heavy.
Asking if they ate is exactly right.
en.editorNote: Send to the family member or friend who never says they miss you but always asks if you've eaten — that's their confession
variations: Short: 'Have you eaten?' is the most East Asian way to say 'I miss you.'
Extended: People who truly care don't ask how you're doing — they ask what you ate today, because they need to confirm you're taking care of yourself.

items.sourceNote: POPBEE韓劇雨中場景敘事套路觀察，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇教會你一件事：
只要開始下雨，
就一定要發生什麼大事。

分手在下雨，
重逢在下雨，
頓悟自己愛上對方也在下雨。

所以現實裡每次下雨，
你都莫名期待轉角會出現一個人
幫你撐傘、什麼都不說。

結果轉角出現的
是一台濺你一身水的公車。

這就是韓劇沒教的續集。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個下雨天總是特別多愁善感、幻想會有劇情發生的朋友
variations: 短版：韓劇裡下雨是伏筆，現實裡下雨是要你記得收衣服。
續集版：真的有人在雨中幫你撐傘的話，先確認他傘往你這邊偏——韓劇男主角的傘永遠是往女主角那邊歪的。

en.content:
K-dramas taught you one thing:
the moment it starts raining,
something major is about to happen.

Breakups in the rain,
reunions in the rain,
realizing you're in love — also in the rain.

So every time it rains in real life,
you half-expect someone to appear around the corner,
hold an umbrella over you, and say nothing.

What actually appears around the corner
is a bus that splashes you head to toe.

That's the sequel the dramas skipped.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend who gets extra sentimental on rainy days and keeps waiting for a plot to happen
variations: Short: In dramas, rain is foreshadowing. In real life, rain means bring your laundry inside.
Sequel: If someone does share their umbrella with you in the rain, check that they're tilting it toward you — the male lead's umbrella always leans the heroine's way.

items.sourceNote: UDN女子漾韓劇「守在原地」台詞情感分析，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
韓劇裡有一種台詞，
聽起來很簡單，
可是會讓你眼眶一熱：

「你不用趕，
我會在這裡等你，
不管多久都可以。」

因為長大以後你才發現，
願意在原地等你的人
真的很少。

大家都急著往前，
急著要你趕上，
急著要你變成他們期待的樣子——

很少有人願意說一句：
慢慢來，我等你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個總是願意等你、從來不催你的人——謝謝他願意留在原地
variations: 短版：「慢慢來，我等你」這六個字，長大後才知道有多難得。
反向版：如果身邊有人願意等你，別把他的等待當理所當然——他不是沒有往前的能力，是選擇了留下來。

en.content:
There's a kind of K-drama line
that sounds simple
but makes your eyes sting:

"Don't rush.
I'll be right here waiting for you,
for as long as it takes."

Because once you grow up, you realize
people willing to wait for you
are genuinely rare.

Everyone's in a hurry to move ahead,
in a hurry for you to catch up,
in a hurry for you to become who they expected —

few are willing to just say:
take your time, I'll wait.
en.editorNote: Send to the person who always waits for you and never rushes you — thank them for staying put
variations: Short: 'Take your time, I'll wait' — you only learn how rare those words are after you grow up.
Flip side: If someone's willing to wait for you, don't take it for granted — they're not incapable of moving ahead, they chose to stay.

items.sourceNote: Dcard追劇板韓劇財閥男主角人設觀察，追劇幻想討論，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
追韓劇久了會有一個副作用：
你的擇偶標準
悄悄被財閥男主角綁架了。

他要高、要冷、
要外表兇但只對你溫柔、
要有一棟能看夜景的房子、
最好還會突然出現在你被欺負的現場。

然後你回到現實，
看著那個約會遲到
還問你「要不要各付各的」的對象——

你才想起：
財閥是編劇寫出來的，
不是你不夠好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個追完劇就開始嫌棄現實對象、標準越來越高的朋友——笑著提醒她那是虛構的
variations: 短版：財閥男主角是編劇寫的，現實裡連準時赴約都是稀有款。
清醒版：與其等一個財閥，不如找一個會準時、會回訊息、吵架願意先低頭的普通人——那才是現實裡的頂配。

en.content:
Watch enough K-dramas and there's a side effect:
your dating standards
get quietly kidnapped by the chaebol male lead.

He has to be tall, aloof,
intimidating to everyone but gentle only with you,
owning a place with a skyline view,
ideally showing up right when someone's giving you a hard time.

Then you return to reality
and look at the date who showed up late
and asked if you two should "just split the bill" —

and you remember:
the chaebol was written by a screenwriter.
It's not that you're not good enough.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend whose standards keep climbing after every drama and who now looks down on real dates — remind her, laughing, that it's fiction
variations: Short: The chaebol lead was written by a screenwriter. In real life, even showing up on time is a rare edition.
Reality check: Instead of waiting for a chaebol, find an ordinary person who's punctual, texts back, and apologizes first after a fight — that's the real-world top-tier model.

items.sourceNote: POPBEE低潮時看的韓劇經典台詞整理，療癒勵志方向，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
有一種韓劇台詞，
是在你以為撐不下去的時候，
輕輕告訴你：

「你現在走的這條隧道很長，
長到你以為外面已經沒有光了。

但沒有一條隧道是沒有出口的。
世界上沒有永遠的黑，
就像沒有永遠的痛。」

看的時候你只覺得台詞寫得好，
直到某天你自己走進那條隧道，
才發現這句話
是有人先替你走過一次，
再回頭來牽你的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個正在低潮、覺得看不到盡頭的朋友——不用多說什麼，這句話會替你陪著他
variations: 短版：沒有一條隧道是沒有出口的，你現在只是還沒走到那個彎。
反向版：如果你已經走出過一次隧道，記得回頭看看——後面可能還有人正卡在最黑的那一段。

en.content:
There's a kind of K-drama line
that finds you right when you think
you can't hold on anymore,
and quietly says:

"The tunnel you're walking through is long —
so long you've convinced yourself
there's no light left outside.

But no tunnel is without an exit.
There's no eternal darkness,
just like there's no eternal pain."

You first think it's just well-written.
Then one day you walk into that tunnel yourself,
and realize the line
was someone who'd already made it through once,
coming back to take your hand.
en.editorNote: Send to the friend stuck in a low point who can't see the end — you don't need to add anything, let the line sit with them
variations: Short: No tunnel is without an exit — you just haven't reached the bend yet.
Flip side: If you've made it out of the tunnel once, look back — someone might still be stuck in the darkest stretch.

items.sourceNote: 電影神搜《壞媽媽》經典台詞整理，只要活著就能活下去主題，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
有些韓劇台詞不華麗，
卻像有人拍拍你的背：

「只要活著，
自然就能這樣活下去。」

不是叫你振作，
不是要你正能量，
只是很平靜地告訴你——

你不用今天就想通所有事，
不用馬上變好、變強、變得沒事，

先吃飯，先睡覺，先活著。
剩下的，日子會慢慢幫你接住。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個把自己逼得很緊、覺得「不能垮」的朋友——允許他今天什麼都不解決也沒關係
variations: 短版：先吃飯，先睡覺，先活著，剩下的日子會慢慢接住你。
延伸版：不是每一天都要有意義，有些日子的任務就只是『撐過去』——這樣就已經很了不起了。

en.content:
Some K-drama lines aren't fancy,
but they land like a hand on your back:

"As long as you're alive,
you'll naturally go on living."

It's not telling you to buck up.
Not asking you to be positive.
It's just calmly saying —

you don't have to figure everything out today.
You don't have to instantly get better, stronger, okay.

First eat. First sleep. First stay alive.
The rest — the days will slowly catch for you.
