zh-tw.content:
韓劇有一種場景我一直很喜歡：

兩個人擠在路邊
用塑膠布圍起來的小攤子裡。

椅子很矮，
桌面只有一點點大，
所以他們不是面對面，
是肩膀貼著肩膀，
一起看著同一條馬路。

然後那個白天
講什麼都回「我沒事」的人，
就在那裡開口了。

你有沒有發現，
最難講的話
幾乎都不是坐在對面講出來的。

是在車上、
在走去車站的那段路上、
在一起洗碗的時候——
兩個人都看著別的地方，
話才滑得出來。

所以下次想聽誰說真話，
先別急著把椅子拉到他對面。

找件事，
跟他並排一下。
zh-tw.editorNote: 想關心一個嘴很硬的人時可以用——比起約他「好好談談」，不如找件事跟他一起做
variations: 短版：有些話不是不敢說，是不敢對著眼睛說。
延伸：這週找那個最近怪怪的人一起走一段路，什麼都別問，走就好。

en.content:
There's a K-drama scene I never get tired of:

two people squeezed into
a little street stall
walled off with plastic sheeting.

The stools are low,
the table barely exists,
so they aren't facing each other.
They're shoulder to shoulder,
both watching the same street.

And then the one who answered
"I'm fine" to everything all day
finally starts talking.

Notice something?

The hardest sentences almost never
come out across a table.

They come out in the car,
on the walk to the station,
over a sink full of dishes —
when both people are looking
somewhere else.

So next time you want the truth
from someone,
don't pull your chair around
to face them.

Find something to do,
and sit beside them instead.
en.editorNote: For checking on someone who deflects everything — skip "let's talk" and find something to do together instead
variations: Short: some things aren't hard to say. They're hard to say to someone's face.
Try this: walk somewhere with the person who's been off lately. Ask nothing. Just walk.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 8 月韓劇片單報導；取韓劇「開場先播結局片段再跳回過去」的敘事慣例，原創改寫成人生觀察

zh-tw.content:
韓劇很愛一種開場：

第一集的前三分鐘，
先讓你看到最後那一幕——
有人在路口回頭，
有人手上握著一封沒寄出去的信，
畫面一黑，
跳回「六個月前」。

所以你從頭到尾
都知道會發生什麼壞事。
但你還是一集一集看下去。

而且很奇怪：
知道結局之後，
中間那些很普通的日子
反而看得更清楚——

他們一起吃的那頓飯、
那句被打斷沒說完的話、
那個當時沒有人覺得珍貴的下午。

現實裡我們其實也常常知道。

知道那份工作待不久，
知道那段關係撐不到明年，
知道有些人終究會走。

可是你還是去了、
還是留了、
還是愛了。

不是你笨。

是有些過程本身就是重點，
它不是為了換到一個好結局
才存在的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在明知會結束卻還捨不得的時候看——把力氣留在過程，別提前替自己收尾
variations: 短版：知道結局，不代表過程白過。
延伸：想一件你「知道不會長久」但很喜歡的事，這禮拜還是去做一次。

en.content:
K-dramas love this opening:

the first three minutes of episode one
show you the last scene —
someone turning back at a crossing,
someone holding a letter
that never got sent —
then the screen goes black
and it cuts to "six months earlier."

So you know the whole time
that something bad is coming.
And you keep watching anyway.

Here's the strange part:
once you know how it ends,
the ordinary stretches in the middle
come into sharper focus —

that one meal together,
that sentence someone got cut off from finishing,
that afternoon nobody thought was precious yet.

We usually know, too.

You know the job won't last.
You know the relationship
won't make it to next year.
You know some people will leave.

And you went anyway.
Stayed anyway.
Loved anyway.

That isn't stupidity.

Some middles are the point.
They don't exist
to buy you a good ending.
en.editorNote: For when you can see the ending coming and still can't let go — spend yourself on the middle instead of closing it early
variations: Short: knowing the ending doesn't make the middle a waste.
Try this: name one thing you love that you know won't last, and do it once more this week.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年韓劇《努力克服自卑的我們》金句整理報導，取「各行各業都要求及格，唯獨做人可以一直被原諒」的核心，原創改寫

zh-tw.content:
有部劇對「無能」
下過一個定義，
我第一次聽的時候愣住：

開店的人端不出一道能吃的菜，
我們說他不適合這行。

教書的人講了三年，
底下沒有一個人聽懂，
我們說他不稱職。

那，
一個人身上
完全找不到一點人味呢？

我們卻很寬容地說：

「他就是個性比較直啦。」
「他沒有惡意，只是不太會講話。」

很奇怪對不對。

每一種身分我們都要求要及格，
只有「做人」這一科
可以一直補考。

而且補了幾十年，
通常也沒有人真的去改考卷。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在被那種「我只是講話直」的人刺到之後看；也可以拿來提醒自己別長成那樣
variations: 短版：每種專業都要求及格，只有做人可以一直補考。
延伸：下次有人用「我個性就這樣」帶過，你可以選擇不接受這個理由。

en.content:
A drama gave a definition of "incompetent"
that stopped me cold:

If you run a kitchen
and can't put out one edible plate,
we say you're in the wrong job.

If you teach for three years
and nobody in the room understands you,
we say you're not up to it.

So what about a person
with no trace of decency in them?

That one we forgive:

"He's just blunt, that's all."
"He doesn't mean anything by it.
He's just bad with words."

Strange, isn't it.

Every role has a passing grade
except being a decent human,
which you can retake forever.

And after a few decades of retakes,
usually nobody bothers
to grade it at all.
en.editorNote: For after someone "just being honest" takes a swing at you — and as a reminder not to become that person
variations: Short: every job has a passing grade. Only being decent gets unlimited retakes.
Try this: the next time someone says "that's just how I am," you're allowed to not accept it as a reason.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 8 月新劇《我的荒糖戀愛》意外同居設定的評論文章；取「看見對方沒整理過的版本」核心原創改寫

zh-tw.content:
八月有部戀愛劇的設定很老套，
但老套得很好用：

兩個人陰錯陽差，
得住在同一個屋簷下。

好看的不是心動那段。

是他們開始看見對方
沒有整理過的版本——

剛起床時聲音是啞的、
心情不好會突然變得很安靜、
碗會泡在水槽裡放到隔天、
生氣的時候不摔門，
只是把話全部收起來。

談感情的前期，
我們其實都在展示：

挑最好看的那張照片、
講最順的那一段人生、
把難相處的部分先收到後面。

但關係真正開始，
是在那些收不住的地方——

對方看到了，
然後說：「喔，好啊。」
沒有要你改。

心動很容易。

被看見了還被留下來，
才是難的那一個。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個看過你最沒形象的樣子、現在還在的人；也提醒自己別在關係裡一直演
variations: 短版：心動不難，難的是被看見沒整理的樣子，對方還在。
延伸：這禮拜對親近的人少修一句話，說實話比說得漂亮更值得練。

en.content:
One of August's romance dramas
runs on a tired setup
that still works:

two people end up
under the same roof by accident.

The good part isn't the butterflies.

It's when they start seeing
the unedited version of each other —

the morning voice,
the way one of them goes quiet
instead of saying they're upset,
the bowl left soaking overnight,
the anger that doesn't slam doors
and just puts all the words away.

Early on, we're all curating:

the best photo,
the smoothest version of our history,
the difficult parts filed
somewhere near the back.

But a relationship actually starts
at the parts you can't file away —

when someone sees them
and says, "okay, sure,"
and doesn't ask you to fix it.

Butterflies are easy.

Being seen unedited
and kept anyway
is the hard one.
en.editorNote: Send it to the person who's seen you at your least presentable and stayed; also a nudge to stop performing with people you're close to
variations: Short: the flutter is easy. Being seen unedited and kept anyway is the hard part.
Try this: say one thing to someone close without polishing it. Honest beats well-phrased.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 8 月 tvN 開播的粉絲題材職場戀愛劇介紹頁；只取「粉絲對喜歡的人有無限寬容」這個現象當發想起點，全文原創，未引用任何劇中台詞

zh-tw.content:
有一種力氣很奇怪。

你可以為一個沒見過面的人
記住他每一個小成就，
在他被罵的那天寫五百字，
說他只是那天狀況不好。

你可以幫他找一百種理由，
而且每一種你都真心相信。

然後你回到自己的事情上——

同一個禮拜，你搞砸一件小事，
你給自己零個理由。

同一句「他只是累了」，
換到自己身上
就變成「我就是不行」。

你不是不會體諒人。

你只是把體諒
全部寄到別的地址去了。

今天挪一點回來。

那個你會替他辯護的標準，
自己也用一次。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個對別人超級寬容、對自己零容忍的朋友；也適合在自己搞砸一件小事、整晚一直重播那段畫面的時候讀
variations: 短版：你替別人找一百個理由的那個本事，今天分一個給自己。
延伸：下次自責之前先問——如果是他做的，你會怎麼說？然後照那句講一次。

en.content:
Five hundred words. That's what you wrote
the day someone you've never met
got torn apart online.

You listed his good years.
You explained the bad night.
You meant every line of it.

Same week, you miss one deadline
by twenty minutes.

Zero words of defense.

"He was tired" becomes
"I'm just not good at this"
the second the subject is you.

You're not bad at understanding people.

You've been mailing all of it
to one address.

Keep some at home today.

The case you'd build for him,
build it once for yourself.
en.editorNote: Send it to the friend who defends everyone except themselves; also worth reading on a night you keep replaying one small mistake
variations: Short: you can list a hundred reasons for someone else. Spend one on yourself today.
Try this: before the next round of self-blame, ask what you'd say if a friend did it. Then say that.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 8 月新劇片單，其中一部是女主角被設局背上罪名的復仇劇；只取「戲裡一定有平反那一集、現實沒有」這個對照原創發想，未引用任何台詞

zh-tw.content:
八月有部復仇劇的起點很痛：

女主角一夜之間
被安上一件她沒做過的事，
然後整個房間退開三步。

這種劇一定好看，
因為你知道會有那一集——

證據攤在桌上、
該講的話被講出來、
那些誤會她的人
一個一個轉過頭。

現實最難的地方就在這裡。

現實沒有那一集。

你被誤會的那件事，
可能到今天還放在
某些人心裡的資料夾，
標題還是錯的，
而你連要對誰解釋都不知道。

所以要換一個算法。

別再等一場
把所有人叫回來的說明會。

去看那三、四個
從頭到尾沒有退開的人。

洗刷不是靠全世界點頭。

是有人在什麼證據都還沒看到的時候
就說：我認識你，這不像你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在被誤會、卻發現怎麼講都沒用的時候讀；也適合傳給那個為了一句不實的話反覆難過好幾天的人
variations: 短版：現實沒有真相攤開的那一集。看那幾個沒有退開的人就好。
延伸：與其寫第七版解釋訊息，不如打給那個一開始就相信你的人。

en.content:
Three steps back. That's what a room does
the moment a rumor lands on you.

August's revenge drama opens right there:
a thing she didn't do,
stuck to her name overnight.

You keep watching because you know
the episode is coming —

evidence on the table,
the truth said out loud,
every doubter turning around,
one by one.

Real life skips that episode.

The thing you were blamed for
is still filed in somebody's head
under the wrong title,
and there's no room to book,
no one left to correct.

So change what you're counting.

Stop waiting for the meeting
that calls everyone back in.

Count the three or four people
who never stepped back at all.

Being cleared isn't a vote.

It's someone saying, before any proof,
that it doesn't sound like you.
en.editorNote: For the stretch when you've been misread and no explanation is landing; also good to send to someone stuck on one untrue sentence
variations: Short: real life skips the episode where the truth comes out. Count who never stepped back.
Try this: instead of drafting explanation number seven, call the person who believed you first.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 8 月韓劇片單報導；由「本月多部作品仍大量使用內心獨白敘事」延伸出的原創觀察，未引用任何劇中台詞或角色

zh-tw.content:
韓劇裡最不公平的一個設計，
是心裡的那句話會被念出來。

男主角走到門口，沒有按電鈴，
站了三秒就走了。

臉上什麼都沒有。

但觀眾聽得到他心裡那句：
今天先不要吵她。

所以你覺得他好體貼。

可是屋子裡的那個人
沒有那條音軌。

她只知道
有人來了，又走了。

我們每天都在做這件事。

心裡整段跑完：
怕她累、怕講出來變壓力、
怕自己聽起來很煩，
所以決定不講。

對方收到的版本是——
他今天很冷淡。

你以為那是體貼，
傳到對面只是一段空白。

現實沒有人幫你配音。

想讓誰知道，就得講。

講得很笨、很短、
完全不像台詞，都可以。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在憋著一句在乎很久、想著「他應該懂吧」的時候讀；也可以在七夕前傳給那個你一直用做的、很少用說的人
variations: 短版：你心裡那段話對方聽不到。他只看到你站了三秒就走。
延伸：這禮拜挑一句你想過但沒說出口的，原封不動講出來，不要先修飾。

en.content:
Three seconds. He stands outside her door
for three seconds, then leaves.

His face gives away nothing.

But you hear the line in his head:
don't bother her tonight.

So you decide he's thoughtful.

The person inside the apartment
never got that audio track.

She knows one thing:
someone came, then went.

We do this all day.

The whole case runs internally —
she's tired, it'll sound like pressure,
I'll come across as a lot —
so nothing gets said.

What lands on the other side
is just: he was cold today.

You call it consideration.
It arrives as a blank.

Nobody is dubbing your inner voice.

If you want someone to know, say it.

Clumsy is fine. Short is fine.
Nothing about it has to sound written.
en.editorNote: For anyone holding in an "I care about you" and hoping it shows; also a nudge before a date night with someone you show up for but rarely tell
variations: Short: nobody hears your inner monologue. They only see you stand there and leave.
Try this: pick one thing you thought but didn't say this week. Say it unpolished.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 8 月 Netflix 韓劇上架清單（同月多部同時開播、觀眾片單塞爆）；取「停在第三集的那幾部」為核心原創發想

zh-tw.content:
打開 App，
最上面那排「繼續觀看」，
有五部停在第三集。

不是難看。

那部你其實還記得——
配樂很好、選角也對，
只是那陣子你剛換工作，
每天回家只想看
不用動腦的東西。

過兩年再點開，
你可能一路看到完，
還會哭。

同一部劇，
換一個時間點看，
會變成完全不一樣的東西。

人也是。

有些人你當時真的接不住。

不是他不好，
也不是你不好，
是那段時間的你
就只剩那麼多力氣。

所以不用急著
把停下來的東西
全部判成失敗。

有些是真的不合。

有些只是——
還沒到你看得下去的那一年。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在為一段沒能繼續下去的關係反覆檢討自己的時候讀；也適合傳給那個把「沒做完」當成人格缺陷的朋友
variations: 短版：停在第三集不代表難看，可能只是那陣子的你只剩那麼多力氣。
延伸：清單裡挑一部當年放掉的，今晚重開第一集，看看現在的你接不接得住。

en.content:
Five titles, all stalled on episode three.
That's your Continue Watching row.

None of them were bad.

You remember that one, actually —
good score, right cast.
You'd just started a new job
and wanted something
that asked nothing of you.

Open it two years later
and you might finish it in a weekend.
You might even cry at it.

Same show, different season of your life,
completely different show.

People work the same way.

Someone you couldn't hold onto back then
wasn't a bad person.
Neither were you.

You had a certain amount of capacity
that year, and that was all of it.

So stop grading everything you stopped.

Some of it was a mismatch.

Some of it was just
a couple of years early.
en.editorNote: For the nights you keep auditing yourself over a relationship that didn't continue; also for the friend who treats "unfinished" as a character flaw
variations: Short: stalled on episode three doesn't mean bad. That season, that was all the capacity you had.
Try this: reopen one show you dropped years ago. See whether this version of you can hold it.

items.sourceNote: 口譯員 × 頂流演員設定的韓劇報導；由「口譯不得替講者修飾」這條職業規範延伸的原創觀察，未引用劇中任何台詞

zh-tw.content:
口譯員有一條規矩，
我第一次看到愣了一下：

不可以幫講者修飾。

對方講得很衝，
你就得衝著翻。
對方講到一半跳針，
你也得跟著跳。

不能加、不能刪，
不能替他把話講得比較好聽。

我們在關係裡剛好相反。

他丟來一句「隨便」，
你自己在後面補上
「他今天大概很累」。

他兩天沒回訊息，
你替他寫好一整段理由。

那不是理解。
那是幫他潤稿。

潤久了會有副作用——

你記得的那個人，
是你修過的版本。

哪天他原封不動
把真正的意思講出來，
你會覺得他變了。

他沒有變。

是你一直在幫他配
一個比較溫柔的聲音。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在替一個人找藉口找到自己都累的時候讀；也適合傳給那個總是說「他不是那個意思」的朋友
variations: 短版：你不是在理解他，你是在幫他潤稿。潤久了，你記得的只是你修過的版本。
延伸：挑一則你會自動幫對方補理由的訊息，只讀字面，不要加上你的旁白。

en.content:
There's a rule interpreters work by,
and it stopped me the first time I heard it:

you don't get to improve the speaker.

If he's blunt, you're blunt.
If he loses the thread, so do you.

Nothing added, nothing cut,
nothing softened on his behalf.

In our own relationships we do the opposite.

He sends back "whatever,"
and you quietly append
"he's had a long week."

Two days of no reply,
and you write him a full defense.

That isn't understanding him.
That's editing him.

Do it long enough and the side effect shows up —

the person you remember
is your edited version.

The day he says what he actually means,
unedited,
you'll decide he's changed.

He hasn't.

You were just dubbing him
in a kinder voice.
en.editorNote: For when you've run out of excuses to make for someone; also for the friend who keeps insisting "that's not how he meant it"
variations: Short: you're not understanding him, you're editing him. The edited version is the one you remember.
Try this: take one message you instantly explained away. Read only the words, no narration.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 9 月 Netflix 韓劇上架清單（九月最受期待的話題新劇是八集短篇）；取「短劇沒有廢戲」為核心原創發想

zh-tw.content:
九月最多人在等的那部，
只有八集。

八集的劇沒有廢戲。

沒有第五集的溫泉旅行，
沒有第七集那場
跟主線完全無關的尾牙。

每一場都得把事情往前推。

拿這個標準看一下你這禮拜：

那個講了三年、每次都只是抱怨的飯局。
那個滑完心情只會更差的帳號。
那個沒人在說話、你卻不敢退的群組。
那件你不想做、只是不想被說難搞的事。

如果你的人生也只有八集，
這些第一個被剪掉。

不是因為它們很糟，
是因為放不下。

十六集的人有本錢慢慢演。

你不知道自己領到幾集，
但至少可以決定
今天這一場要不要留。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在行事曆滿到喘不過氣、卻說不出哪一件真的重要的時候讀；也可以在回覆下一個邀約之前先看一次
variations: 短版：八集的劇沒有廢戲。你不知道自己領到幾集，先想想今天這一場要不要留。
延伸：把這禮拜的行程念一遍，挑一個「剪掉也不會怎樣」的，這次真的剪掉。

en.content:
The most-anticipated September title
runs eight episodes.

Eight episodes means no filler.

No hot-spring trip in episode five.
No office party in episode seven
that has nothing to do with anything.

Every scene has to move something.

Run your week past that standard:

The dinner you've kept for three years that's only ever complaining.
The account that leaves you worse off every time you scroll it.
The group chat nobody posts in that you're afraid to leave.
The favor you don't want to do and only do to avoid seeming difficult.

If your life were eight episodes,
those get cut first.

Not because they're terrible.
Because there's no room.

Sixteen-episode people can afford a slow middle.

You don't know your episode count.
You do get to decide
whether today's scene stays in.
en.editorNote: For a week that's fully booked and still feels like nothing important is on it; good to read before you answer the next invite
variations: Short: eight episodes means no filler. You don't know your episode count, so decide whether today's scene earns its place.
Try this: read your week out loud, find the one thing nobody would miss, and actually cut it.

items.sourceNote: 下半年待播劇的角色海報消息（不想當人類的九尾狐與人類戀愛的設定）；對白與內文皆為原創撰寫，未引用劇中任何台詞

zh-tw.content:
下半年有部劇的設定，
是一個活了很久的東西，
愛上一個會老的人。

我在腦內幫他們寫了一段對話——

「你們人類最麻煩的是什麼？」
「會過期。」

「那最好的呢？」
「也是會過期。」

「所以？」
「所以我今天想講的話，
不能留到以後。」

「我可以等你。」
「可是我不行啊。」

活很久的那一方，
最後學會的不是永恆，
是急。

那種急一點都不難看。

它長得像：
還沒吵完就先講和、
想到就打電話、
把「以後再說」
改成「現在就說」。

會結束的人，
才需要現在。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在一直把重要的話往後排的時候讀；也適合傳給那個你老是想著「改天再約」的人
variations: 短版：會結束的人，才需要現在。
延伸：把一句你打算「以後再說」的話今天講完，不用挑好時機。

en.content:
A show later this year puts something ancient
in love with someone who ages.

I wrote them a conversation in my head —

"What's the worst thing about humans?"
"We expire."

"And the best?"
"Also that."

"Meaning?"
"Meaning what I want to say today
can't wait for later."

"I can wait for you."
"I can't."

What the immortal one finally learns
isn't patience.

It's urgency.

And urgency looks better than people think.

It looks like:
ending the argument early,
calling the second you think of them,
turning "sometime" into "tonight."

Only things that end
need a right now.
en.editorNote: For anyone stacking important sentences behind a better moment; send it to the person you keep meaning to see
variations: Short: only things that end need a right now.
Try this: say the thing you were saving for later, today, without waiting for the timing to be good.

items.sourceNote: 2026 韓劇待播片單整理（含吸血鬼與畫家的奇幻愛情設定）；由「拍不下來的人只能靠人記住」延伸的原創短文，未引用劇中台詞

zh-tw.content:
待播清單裡有個設定我一直記著：

一個不會出現在任何照片裡的人，
和一個負責把他畫下來的人。

拍不到，就只能用看的。
看得不夠仔細，就畫不出來。

我們剛好相反。

一頓飯拍了幾十張，
一張都沒再打開過。

有些人在你身邊很多年，
你卻說不出
他笑的時候哪一邊會先動。

真正記得一個人，
跟你存了幾張照片無關。

是他不在的時候，
你還畫得出來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在滑完相簿卻覺得空空的時候讀；也可以當成提醒——今天這頓飯先把手機放下
variations: 短版：真正記得一個人，是他不在的時候你還畫得出來。
延伸：今天跟誰吃飯就不要拍，回家試著描述他穿什麼、笑的時候先動哪一邊。

en.content:
One setup on the upcoming list stuck with me:

a man who never shows up in a photograph,
and the painter who has to record him.

No camera, so you look.
Look carelessly and the painting fails.

We run the opposite way.

Thirty photos from one dinner,
not one of them opened again.

Someone can be around for years
and you still couldn't say
which side of their face moves first
when they smile.

Remembering a person
has nothing to do with your storage.

It's whether you could draw them
when they're not in the room.
en.editorNote: For scrolling a camera roll that somehow feels empty; also a nudge to put the phone down at dinner tonight
variations: Short: remembering someone is whether you could draw them when they're not in the room.
Try this: photograph nothing at dinner tonight, then describe later what they wore and how they laughed.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 8 月韓劇開播清單（含假戀人／假裝交往設定的浪漫喜劇）；由「假裝」這個梗延伸的原創短句，未引用任何劇中台詞

zh-tw.content:
假裝在一起，是演給別人看的。
假裝沒喜歡上，是每天演給自己看一次。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合曖昧期還在嘴硬的時候，或傳給那個明明在意卻裝沒事的人
variations: 短版：最累的不是喜歡，是每天把喜歡收起來。
延伸：如果收得那麼辛苦，那不是不喜歡，是還沒決定要不要說。

en.content:
Pretending to date is a performance for other people.
Pretending you haven't fallen is one you put on for yourself, every single day.
en.editorNote: For the stage where you're still denying it, or for the friend who's clearly into someone and pretending otherwise
variations: Short: liking someone isn't the tiring part. Putting it away every day is.
Try this: if hiding it takes that much work, it isn't indifference. It's an unmade decision.

items.sourceNote: 2026 韓劇產業觀察（卡司組合與角色配置的趨勢討論）；由「戲份多寡」延伸的原創短句，非任何劇的台詞

zh-tw.content:
在別人的故事裡，你是路人。
沒關係。你那部戲，鏡頭從第一秒就沒離開過你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在覺得自己可有可無的日子讀，或傳給總是先讓位給別人的朋友
variations: 短版：別人的故事裡沒你的戲份，不代表你的故事沒開拍。
延伸：今天做一件完全不會被看到的事，只因為你自己想做。

en.content:
In someone else's story you're an extra.
That's fine. In your own, the camera has never once left you.
en.editorNote: For a day when you feel skippable, or for the friend who always steps aside first
variations: Short: no screen time in someone else's story doesn't mean yours hasn't started.
Try this: do one thing today nobody will see, purely because you wanted to.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 8 月底開播的藝術高中題材新劇介紹（校園起點、延伸到成年）；由校園劇的轉學生鏡頭延伸的原創短文，未引用劇情或台詞

zh-tw.content:
韓劇裡的轉學生，第一天都有同一顆鏡頭：
門一開，全班回頭。

現實的開學沒有那顆鏡頭。
你進教室、找位子、坐下，
沒有人特別看你。

以前覺得可惜。
現在覺得那是好消息——

沒人盯著的時候，
你才可以慢慢變成
你想要的樣子，
不用第一天就到位。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合開學前一週睡不著的時候讀，也可以傳給要換環境的人
variations: 短版：沒有人回頭看你，是好消息——你可以慢慢變。
延伸：新環境的第一週先別急著定義自己，讓自己安靜地存在幾天。

en.content:
The transfer student in every K-drama gets the same shot on day one:
the door opens, the whole class turns around.

Real first days don't come with that shot.
You walk in, find a seat, sit down.
Nobody looks up.

That used to feel like a loss.
Now it reads as good news —

when nobody is watching,
you get to become
whoever you're going for
slowly, instead of landing it on day one.
en.editorNote: For the week before a new term when you can't sleep; also for anyone about to change environments
variations: Short: nobody turning to look is good news. It means you can change slowly.
Try this: don't define yourself in week one of anything new. Just exist quietly for a few days.

items.sourceNote: 2026 韓劇片單整理（含離島醫療題材新劇）；由「小島唯一一間診所」延伸的原創短文，未引用劇情或台詞

zh-tw.content:
八月有部醫療劇的設定很單純：
一個醫生，一座島，一間診所。

那裡沒有分科。
感冒、扭傷、半夜肚子痛，
全部都是他。

我想到身邊那幾個人。

他們也不是照規格配來的——
有人不太會安慰，
有人只會默默幫你買晚餐。

難過的時候，
他們就是島上全部的資源。

不夠專業，但都到場了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在覺得沒人真的懂你的時候讀，也提醒自己別因為對方不會安慰就否定他
variations: 短版：他們不夠專業，但都到場了。
延伸：今天回訊息給那個很少講漂亮話、卻總是出現的人。

en.content:
One of August's medical dramas has a simple setup:
one doctor, one island, one clinic.

No departments out there.
Colds, sprained ankles, a stomach that turns at 2am —
all of it is him.

It made me think about my own few people.

They didn't arrive to spec either —
one of them is bad at comforting anyone,
one of them just quietly buys you dinner.

On a bad night,
they are the entire supply on the island.

Not qualified. But present.
en.editorNote: For nights when you feel like nobody really gets you; also a reminder not to write off someone who's just bad at comforting
variations: Short: they're not qualified. But they showed up.
Try this: message the person who never says the right thing and always turns up anyway.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 8 月韓劇片單整理；由韓劇常見的「共撐一把傘」鏡頭語言延伸的原創短句，未引用任何劇的台詞

zh-tw.content:
他從來沒說喜歡你。
他只是把傘偏過來，讓自己濕掉那半邊。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種嘴上什麼都不說、卻總是先讓你的人，也適合自己看懂之後存下來
variations: 短版：他沒說喜歡你，他只是讓自己濕了那半邊。
延伸：今天回想一下，最近有誰替你擋了什麼卻沒講。

en.content: He never said he liked you. He just tilted the umbrella your way and let his own shoulder take the rain.
en.editorNote: For the person who never says it out loud but always shifts to cover you first
variations: Short: he didn't say it. He just let his own shoulder get soaked.
Try this: think about who took a hit for you lately without mentioning it.

items.sourceNote: 韓劇觀察類文章（角色相處細節的討論）；由餐桌上的小動作延伸的原創短句，非任何劇的台詞

zh-tw.content:
他不太會講漂亮話。
他只是每次都先把太辣的那盤，移到你搆不到的地方。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在覺得對方不夠浪漫的時候讀，提醒自己有些在乎是用手做的
variations: 短版：他不會講，他只是每次都先把那盤移開。
延伸：下次吃飯的時候，留意誰先動了桌上的東西。

en.content: He's not good with words. He just slides the too-spicy dish out of your reach first, every single time.
en.editorNote: For when you're tempted to call someone unromantic — some care only shows up as hands
variations: Short: he can't say it, so he moves the plate instead.
Try this: at your next meal, notice who rearranges the table before anyone asks.

items.sourceNote: 韓劇報導（浪漫劇集的場面討論）；由「送到家」這個鏡頭延伸的原創短句，未引用劇情台詞

zh-tw.content:
喜歡一個人最安靜的證據：
送你到家之後，他還有一整段路要自己走。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在曖昧期分不清對方心意的時候讀，也可以傳給那個總是繞遠路的人
variations: 短版：他送你到家，然後一個人把那段路再走一次。
延伸：想想看有誰為了見你，多走了不必要的路。

en.content: The quietest proof someone likes you: after walking you home, he still has the whole way back to walk alone.
en.editorNote: For the stage where you can't read someone's intentions yet, or for the friend who always takes the long way
variations: Short: he walked you home, then walked all of it again by himself.
Try this: count who has gone out of their way just to see you.

items.sourceNote: 2026 韓劇產業觀察（角色塑造與情感表達方式的討論）；由「動作先於台詞」的敘事手法延伸的原創短句

zh-tw.content:
有些人的告白，語言永遠是最後才到。
手先到，外套先到，人先到。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在等一句話等到懷疑人生的時候讀，先看看對方的動作已經說了什麼
variations: 短版：話最後才到，人早就到了。
延伸：與其等他開口，先數一數他已經做過的事。

en.content: For some people the words always arrive last. The hands get there first. Then the jacket. Then the person.
en.editorNote: For when you're still waiting on a sentence — check what their actions already said
variations: Short: the words come last. The person got there ages ago.
Try this: instead of waiting for him to speak, count what he's already done.

items.sourceNote: 2026 上半年熱議韓劇整理（觀眾對演員情緒戲表現的討論）；由哭戲收音細節延伸的原創內容

zh-tw.content:
韓劇的哭戲，麥克風先收到的不是哭聲。
是吸氣。

那一下很短，
把空氣往回吸的那個聲音。
厲害的演員都先讓它漏出來，
觀眾才知道他快撐不住了。

現實裡也有這個聲音。

電話那頭本來講得好好的，
中間突然停半拍，吸了一下，
然後說「就那樣啊，還好啦」。

你不用戳破。
也不用趕快換一個輕鬆的話題。

把話停在那裡，多等三秒就好。

很多人缺的不是安慰。
是有人聽見那一下之後，
沒有急著把場子救回來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在講電話時聽到對方聲音突然變一下的當下讀，提醒自己先安靜幾秒再開口
variations: 短版：他還沒哭，但你已經聽到那一下吸氣了。那時候別急著講話。
延伸：下次對方說「還好啦」，你可以只回一句「我在」，然後閉嘴等他。

en.content:
In a K-drama crying scene, the mic picks up the breath before it picks up the crying.

Just that one short intake of air. Good actors let it slip out first — that's how you know they're about to lose it.

You've heard that sound in real life too. Someone on the phone is talking fine, then there's half a beat, a small breath, and they say "nah, I'm okay, it's whatever."

You don't have to call them out. You also don't have to rush in with a lighter topic.

Just leave the silence there. Three more seconds.

What most people are missing isn't comfort. It's someone who hears that breath and doesn't immediately try to rescue the mood.
en.editorNote: For the moment on a call when their voice shifts — a reminder to stay quiet a few seconds longer
variations: Short: they haven't cried yet, but you heard the breath. That's the part where you stop talking.
Try this: next time they say "I'm fine," just say "I'm here" and wait.

items.sourceNote: 2026 上半年韓劇盤點（台詞與人物關係討論）；由韓語慣用「우리（我們）」代替「我的」的語言習慣延伸的原創內容

zh-tw.content:
「我們家那個啊——」

韓劇裡這句話出現太多次，
多到你會忘記它其實很怪。

韓文裡幾乎不講「我的」。
我們家、我們公司、我們學校，
連自己的老公都叫「我們老公」。

第一次聽會想吐槽：
那是你老公，又不是大家的。

後來覺得這個用法很厲害。

「我的」是所有權。
「我們的」是把一個人拉進圈子裡，
順便對外面宣布：
這個有人罩。

回想一下自己被改口的那一次。

人家本來介紹你是「這是我同事」，
某天變成「我們那個誰誰」。

沒有通知，你也記不得是哪一天。
但被歸進「我們」之後，
你在外面就不算一個人了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在覺得自己是外人的日子讀，也可以在把某個朋友正式改口叫「我們家的」時傳給他
variations: 短版：從「我朋友」變成「我們那個」，沒有儀式，但那天你就有人罩了。
延伸：今天挑一個人，講到他的時候故意用「我們」，看他有沒有發現。

en.content:
"Oh, our guy at home —"

That line shows up so often in K-dramas you stop noticing how strange it is.

Korean barely uses "my." It's our house, our company, our school. People even call their own husband "our husband."

The first time you hear it you want to argue. That's your husband. He is not communal property.

Then it starts to seem clever.

"Mine" is ownership. "Ours" pulls a person inside a circle and announces to everyone outside: this one is covered.

Think about the time someone changed how they said your name. You used to be "this is my coworker." Then one day you were "that's our person."

Nobody announced it. You couldn't name the day. But once you got filed under "ours," you stopped being out there alone.
en.editorNote: For a day you feel like an outsider — or send it to the friend you've started calling one of ours
variations: Short: going from "my friend" to "our guy" has no ceremony. It just means someone's got you now.
Try this: pick one person today and say "ours" when you mention them. See if they catch it.

items.sourceNote: 2026 韓劇片單整理（常見場景與人物設定討論）；由汗蒸幕場景的功能延伸的原創內容

zh-tw.content:
幾乎每部韓劇都會去一次汗蒸幕。

進去以後，所有人換上同一套短袖短褲，
毛巾在頭上捲成兩隻角，
一排人躺在地板上。

那個地方沒辦法炫耀。

財閥的兒子跟隔壁大嬸，
躺著看起來差不多。

所以編劇很愛把最難講的那段對話
放在這裡——
因為在裡面，
誰都穿不上自己的身分。

你那幾個真的能講心裡話的朋友，
多半也不是在會議室認識的。

是在宿舍、在搬家那天、
在走廊上陪你坐了一整晚的人。

關係要變深，
通常得先有一個場合，
把兩邊的裝備都拿掉。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在覺得跟誰一直卡在客套層的時候讀，想一下有沒有機會約一件會弄髒衣服的事
variations: 短版：穿著全套裝備的人，講不出真話。
延伸：想跟誰更熟，別約吃高級的。約搬家、約爬山、約一起把事情弄亂。

en.content:
Almost every K-drama makes one trip to the sauna house.

Everyone changes into the same shirt and shorts, folds a towel into two little horns on their head, and lies down in a row on the floor.

There's nothing to show off with in there. The chaebol's son and the auntie next to him look about the same lying down.

So writers love putting the hardest conversation in that room. Inside it, nobody gets to wear their status.

The few friends you can actually say things to — you probably didn't meet them in a conference room. You met in a dorm, on moving day, in a hallway where someone sat with you all night.

Getting close usually needs a setting that strips the gear off both people first.
en.editorNote: For when a friendship is stuck at the polite layer — think of one plan that would get your clothes dirty
variations: Short: people in full armor can't say true things.
Try this: to get closer to someone, don't book the nice dinner. Help them move.

items.sourceNote: 韓國生日習俗介紹（生日喝海帶湯的由來與產後飲食關聯）；結合韓劇常見餐桌場景改寫的原創內容

zh-tw.content:
追久了會發現，
韓劇的鍋子裡大概只有三種湯。

生日早上的海帶湯——
那碗不是在慶祝你，
是你媽生完你那陣子喝的同一種。

宿醉隔天的解酒湯——
端上來的時候，
昨天那些事一句都不會被提。

還有誰終於回家那天，
爐上一直溫著的大醬湯。

沒有一鍋是因為好吃才煮的。

煮的人是拿湯在記日子：
你哪天出生、
你哪天撐不住、
你哪天肯回來。

所以你可能忘了去年生日誰講了什麼，
卻還記得那天家裡有沒有開火。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在生日前後或很久沒回家的時候讀，也可以在自己煮東西給別人吃之前看一眼
variations: 短版：湯是一種行事曆。他不是在煮飯，是在記你的日子。
延伸：這禮拜找一天為某個人開一次火，什麼理由都不用給。

en.content:
Watch enough K-dramas and you notice the pot only ever holds three soups.

The seaweed soup on your birthday morning. That bowl isn't celebrating you — it's the same soup your mother lived on the weeks after she had you.

The hangover soup the next day. When it lands on the table, nobody brings up last night.

And the stew that's been kept warm on the stove for whoever finally came home.

Not one of them was cooked because it tastes good.

Whoever cooks is keeping a calendar in soup: the day you were born, the day you couldn't hold it together, the day you agreed to come back.

You probably forgot what anyone said at last year's birthday. You still remember whether someone turned the stove on.
en.editorNote: For birthday week, or a stretch where you haven't gone home — read it before you cook for someone
variations: Short: soup is a calendar. They're not cooking. They're keeping track of your days.
Try this: turn the stove on for one person this week. No occasion required.

items.sourceNote: 2026 上半年韓劇口碑盤點（含資深主角偽裝成新人臥底的職場劇設定）；取其設定核心改寫的原創內容

zh-tw.content:
一個做了十幾年的老手，
因為長了一張看不出年紀的臉，
被派去混進新人堆裡重新來一次。

他很快就發現，
真正難的是裝作自己還不會——
看到旁邊的人把步驟做反，
手伸出去一半又收回來，
改成問一句「這個要怎麼弄啊」。

這件事其實很多人每天都在做：
把已經想到的答案吞回去，
等資淺的那個人自己講出來。

忍住不救，有時候比出手還累。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合帶新人帶到快沒耐性的時候讀，也可以傳給那個什麼都自己扛、不敢放手的組長
variations: 短版：帶人最累的部分不在教，在等。
延伸：這禮拜挑一件你三分鐘能解決的小事，讓對方花三十分鐘自己做完。

en.content:
A veteran with fifteen years in the job gets sent back to the bottom, planted among the new hires because his face reads a decade younger than his résumé.

He finds out fast that pretending to be young is easy. Pretending he doesn't know how is the hard part — watching someone run the steps backward, getting his hand halfway out, pulling it back, and asking "wait, how does this part work?" instead.

Plenty of people do a version of this every day: swallowing the answer they already have so the junior person can arrive at it out loud.

Not rescuing someone costs more energy than rescuing them.
en.editorNote: For when you're out of patience training someone — or send it to the lead who takes on everything because letting go feels slower
variations: Short: the tiring part of mentoring isn't teaching. It's waiting.
Try this: pick one thing you could finish in three minutes and let someone else take thirty.

items.sourceNote: 2026 韓劇劇情與人物整理（常見的手機畫面過場鏡頭）；由聯絡人備註變化延伸的原創內容

zh-tw.content:
韓劇有個一秒就過的鏡頭，
很多人會特地倒回去看：
手機螢幕上那個名字。

第三集是全名加職稱，
第十集職稱不見了，
第十四集剩下一個字，
吵架那集又被改回全名，
而整齣戲沒有一句台詞解釋過這件事。

你自己的通訊錄裡也有一模一樣的紀錄，
只是沒有人幫你配樂。

改備註的那天通常什麼都沒發生，
你只是在某個瞬間覺得，
這樣叫他比較順。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在關係正在悄悄變化、但誰都還沒說破的時候讀；也適合翻到某個很久沒改的舊備註時
variations: 短版：關係的進度條不在對話裡，在通訊錄裡。
延伸：現在打開手機，看有沒有哪個備註早就跟你們現在的樣子對不上了。

en.content:
K-dramas have a one-second shot people rewind for: the name on someone's phone screen.

Episode three it's the full name plus a job title. Episode ten the title is gone. Episode fourteen it's down to one syllable. The fight episode, it goes back to the full name — and not one line of dialogue ever mentions it.

Your contacts list keeps the same record. Nobody scores yours with music.

Nothing happens on the day you edit a contact name. You just decide, somewhere in the middle of an ordinary afternoon, that calling them that fits better now.
en.editorNote: For a relationship that's quietly shifting before anyone has said so — or the moment you scroll past a nickname you never updated
variations: Short: the progress bar of a relationship isn't in the messages. It's in the contact name.
Try this: open your phone and find one saved name that no longer matches what you actually are to each other.

items.sourceNote: 2026 上半年熱議韓劇整理（餐桌戲的情緒處理討論）；結合分手前那一餐的場景改寫的原創內容

zh-tw.content:
韓劇的分手很少發生在路上，
通常是一張桌子。

兩個人都知道等一下要講什麼，
但還是先把這頓吃完——
「湯要冷了」、
「你那個藥還有在吃嗎」、
「這個你不是不吃嗎，給我」，
全是廢話，一句正題都沒有。

他們只是在把最後一次
照顧對方的機會用完。

後來你會發現，
最難受的不是那句分手，
是那句話出口之前，
對面還很習慣地
把你不吃的洋蔥挑到旁邊。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在一段感情快到終點、卻還很溫柔的那幾天讀；也適合看完某場餐桌戲久久沒關掉的時候
variations: 短版：他還在幫你挑洋蔥，只是這次是最後一次。
延伸：分開的方式會被記很久。能好好吃完最後一頓的人，通常也不會把彼此講得太難聽。

en.content:
K-drama breakups rarely happen on a street. They happen at a table.

Both of them know what's coming, and they still finish the meal first — "your soup's getting cold," "are you still taking those pills," "you don't eat this, give it here." Nothing but small talk. Not one line about the actual thing.

They're just using up the last chance to take care of each other.

The part that stays with you isn't the sentence that ends it. It's the minute before, when the person across from you is still automatically moving the onions you don't eat to the side of your plate.
en.editorNote: For the strangely gentle days near the end of something — or when a dinner scene leaves you staring at a paused screen
variations: Short: he's still picking the onions out. It's just the last time.
Try this: how something ends gets remembered longer than how it went. People who can finish the last meal rarely trash each other afterward.

items.sourceNote: 2026 韓劇推薦片單（重刷與細節討論）；由二刷時注意到的背景角色延伸的原創內容

zh-tw.content:
第二次看的時候，
你才會看到第一次完全沒看到的東西。

第一集那場吵架，
鏡頭一直對著吵得最兇的兩個人，
但畫面右邊那個角落，
有人站在那裡從頭到尾沒講一句話，
只是安靜地把桌上的杯子
往裡面推了一下，
怕誰揮手打翻。

第一次看的時候，
你的眼睛跟著聲音大的人走。

身邊也有這種人，
他從來不在你記得的畫面正中間，
但你每次回想那段日子，
他都在。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在想起某個一直沒被你好好謝過的人時讀；也可以直接傳給那個人，什麼都不用多說
variations: 短版：真正陪過你的人，很少出現在你記得的畫面中間。
延伸：今天想一個從沒跟你討過功勞的人，跟他說一件你其實一直記得的小事。

en.content:
On a rewatch you finally see what you missed the first time.

That argument in episode one — the camera stays on the two people yelling, but in the right corner of the frame, someone stands there without a single line, quietly nudging the cups toward the middle of the table so nobody knocks one over mid-gesture.

The first time through, your eyes follow whoever is loudest.

You know someone like that. They're never in the center of the scenes you remember, and yet every time you think back to that stretch of your life, they were there.
en.editorNote: For when you think of someone you never properly thanked — you can also just forward it to them with nothing added
variations: Short: the people who actually stayed are rarely in the center of the frame you remember.
Try this: think of someone who never asked for credit, and tell them one small thing you still remember.

items.sourceNote: 2026 韓國影視產業與製作趨勢分析；由拍攝季節與播出季節落差延伸的原創內容

zh-tw.content:
你在冬天哭的那場雪戲，
很可能是八月拍的。

演員穿三層大衣站在三十幾度的巷子裡，
嘴裡含著冰塊才呵得出白氣，
喊卡之後所有人衝去搶電風扇，
下一顆鏡頭再回去繼續發抖。

播出來的時候，
你只覺得那天好冷、他好可憐。

很多看起來剛剛好的東西，
其實都是在完全不對的季節裡，
一格一格湊出來的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在覺得自己現在的努力跟現況完全對不上的時候讀，八月做的事不一定要在八月看到成果
variations: 短版：你現在拍的，是要在很久以後才播的那一集。
延伸：別人看到的是成品那一秒。你在做的是三十幾度那一天。

en.content:
That snow scene you cried at in December was probably shot in August.

The actor stands in a back alley in ninety-degree heat wearing three coats, holding ice in his mouth so his breath will fog, and the second they call cut everyone sprints for the fans — then goes back to shivering for the next take.

By the time it airs, all you feel is how cold that night must have been.

A lot of things that look perfectly timed were assembled frame by frame in completely the wrong season.
en.editorNote: For when what you're working on feels out of sync with where you are — August work doesn't have to pay off in August
variations: Short: what you're shooting now is an episode that airs much later.
Try this: people see the finished second. You're living the ninety-degree afternoon.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 8 月韓劇新作片單（藝術高中音樂青春劇）；由對手兼搭檔的設定延伸的原創對白

zh-tw.content:
「合奏的時候，你為什麼一直盯著我的手？」

「因為你會偷偷變慢，我得跟著慢下來。」

「那你以後別跟了。」

「不行，四隻手只有一首曲子。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 對手跟搭檔坐在同一張琴椅上，是青春劇最好用的設定
variations: 短版：你變慢的時候我也慢了，這件事我一直沒說。
延伸：真正的默契，是連你失誤的節奏我都記得。

en.content:
"Why do you keep staring at my hands when we play?"

"Because you slow down when nobody's listening, and I have to slow down with you."

"Then stop following me."

"Can't do that, four hands only get one song."
en.editorNote: A rival and a partner sharing one piano bench is the best setup a youth drama has
variations: Short: you slowed down and so did I, and I never mentioned it.
Try this: real chemistry is knowing the rhythm of someone's mistakes.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 8 月回歸的刑偵動作續集劇報導；由續集開局套路延伸的原創觀察

zh-tw.content:
續集第一集有三件事一定會發生。

上一季最後那顆鏡頭會原封不動再播一次，旁邊多補一句你沒聽過的台詞。

一個新來的上司走進辦公室，把前一個人桌上的東西收進紙箱。

主角在頂樓點了一根菸，鏡頭轉開之前都不會抽完。
zh-tw.editorNote: 續集的第一集是複習課，順便告訴你這次少了誰
variations: 短版：回歸的第一集，都在告訴你誰沒回來。
延伸：續集最重要的一場戲，通常發生在沒有人坐的那個位子旁邊。

en.content:
Three things always happen in the first episode of a sequel season.

The final shot from last season plays again, this time with one extra line you never heard.

A new boss walks into the office and boxes up everything left on the old desk.

The lead lights a cigarette on the roof and never finishes it before the camera cuts away.
en.editorNote: The first episode of a sequel is a review session that also tells you who's missing this time
variations: Short: every return episode is really about who didn't come back.
Try this: the key scene of a sequel usually happens next to an empty chair.

items.sourceNote: 2026 韓劇新作總覽（身分被冒用題材）；由被奪走姓名的設定延伸的原創擬人書寫

zh-tw.content:
我是你的名字，被人拿走已經三年了。

他用我簽合約、訂位子，在頒獎典禮上被念出來的也是我。

只有一件事他學不會，就是你媽從小把我最後一個音拉得很長。

我還在等你回來，把那個音發對。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在覺得自己的位置被別人占走的時候讀，能把你的名字念對的只有你
variations: 短版：他可以用你的名字，念不出你媽念的那個音。
延伸：能被模仿的東西很多，語尾那一下模仿不來。

en.content:
I am your name, and someone walked off with me three years ago.

He signs contracts with me, books restaurant tables with me, and hears me announced at award shows.

There is one thing he never learned, the way your mom always stretched my last syllable.

I'm still waiting for you to come back and say it right.
en.editorNote: For when it feels like someone else took your spot, only you can say your own name the right way
variations: Short: he can use your name but not the way your mother said it.
Try this: people can copy almost everything except the ending.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 8 月配信的失憶題材愛情喜劇資訊；由失憶與自稱伴侶的設定延伸的原創內容

zh-tw.content:
如果你明天醒過來，腦袋裡一片空白，門口站著一個人說他是你男友，你要怎麼確認？

不要問你們是怎麼認識的，那種故事最好編。

問他你最討厭吃什麼，問他你哭的時候要抱還是不要碰。

如果這兩題他都答得出來，就先讓他進門吧。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合用來想清楚一段關係裡誰真的有在看你，記得的細節比故事誠實
variations: 短版：會編故事的人很多，記得你不吃什麼的沒幾個。
延伸：問他你哭的時候要抱還是不要，答案騙不了人。

en.content:
If you woke up tomorrow with nothing in your head and someone at the door claiming to be your boyfriend, how would you check?

Don't ask how the two of you met, because that part is the easiest thing to invent.

Ask what food you refuse to eat, and ask whether you want to be held when you cry.

If he gets both of those right, go ahead and let him in for now.
en.editorNote: A good filter for who has actually been paying attention, small details are more honest than big stories
variations: Short: plenty of people can tell a good story, few remember what you won't eat.
Try this: ask what you need when you cry, that answer can't be faked.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 8 月回歸的財閥出身刑警搭檔題材報導；由財閥三代進重案組的設定延伸的原創內容

zh-tw.content:
這台新來的，出廠設定就是有錢，別在飯局上跟他搶結帳，搶不贏。

使用前請確認電源，他一整天沒吃東西的時候，判斷力會掉得很明顯。

保固範圍包含在現場擋在你前面、包含替你跟上面吵一架，不包含幫你寫結案報告。

保固期限那一欄是空白的，因為填表的人打算一直修下去。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合形容那種很難搞卻很罩的新同事，用說明書口吻講隊友之間的默契
variations: 短版：他的保固期限那一欄，一直沒有人填。
延伸：會擋在你前面的人，不用寫進職務說明也會做。

en.content:
The new guy ships rich out of the box, so don't race him to the check at dinner, you will not win.

Check the power source before you deploy him, because his judgment drops hard when he hasn't eaten all day.

Coverage includes standing in front of you at a scene and picking a fight with the brass on your behalf, and it does not include writing your case report.

The warranty expiration field is blank, because whoever filled out the form intends to keep servicing this thing indefinitely.
en.editorNote: For the coworker who is a pain and still has your back, written like a product manual
variations: Short: nobody ever filled in his warranty expiration date.
Try this: the guy who steps in front of you never had it in his job description.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 8 月上線的拳擊教練同居戀愛劇評論；由拳擊館場景延伸的原創內容

zh-tw.content:
拳擊館的計時鈴每三分鐘響一次。

他挑在剩十秒的時候開口，說有件事他想了很久，今天不講會後悔，就是關於他每次來這裡真正的……

鈴響了，全館的人同時停下來喝水，他也跟著喝了一口。

下一輪開始前，她把護具遞過來。

她說你剛剛那句話，打完這輪再講一次，我等你。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合形容差一點就說出口的心意，被打斷不代表那句話不算數
variations: 短版：他那句話被鈴聲切斷，她記得比他還清楚。
延伸：講到一半停下來的那句，通常最真。

en.content:
The gym timer goes off every three minutes.

He waits until there are ten seconds left, then says there's something he's been sitting on for months, something about the real reason he keeps coming to this…

The bell cuts him off, the whole gym stops for water, and he takes a sip too.

Before the next round she hands him his headgear.

She says whatever you started back there, finish it when this round is over, I'll wait.
en.editorNote: For the thing you almost said out loud, getting cut off doesn't make it count for less
variations: Short: the bell took his sentence, she kept it anyway.
Try this: the line that gets interrupted is usually the honest one.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 8 月韓劇清單報導；由完結追劇心情延伸的原創內容

zh-tw.content:
想在最終回忍住不哭，方法我教你，把燈全部打開，音量轉到最小，衛生紙放在拿不到的地方。

片頭一下就先去洗碗，回來剛好跳過那段回憶畫面。

眼眶開始發熱的時候，就低頭滑手機，滑到那顆鏡頭過去為止。

這套我用了六年，成功率到目前為止是零，但每次照做，我好像就比較敢按下播放。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在追完一部很難放下的劇之後自嘲，明知沒用還是會做的小儀式
variations: 短版：防哭措施做好做滿，最後還是哭得最大聲。
延伸：成功率是零的儀式，還是幫你把播放鍵按了下去。

en.content:
Here is how to get through a finale without crying: turn every light on, drop the volume, put the tissues somewhere you can't reach.

Go wash the dishes the second the opening theme starts, and you'll come back right after the flashback montage.

When your eyes start to sting, look down at your phone and scroll until that shot is over.

Six years I've run this system, success rate zero, and it is still the thing that gets me to press play.
en.editorNote: For laughing at yourself after a show you can't shake, the useless ritual you do anyway
variations: Short: full anti-crying protocol deployed, still sobbed the loudest.
Try this: a ritual with a zero success rate still got you to press play.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 8 月韓劇推薦整理；由深夜返家的收尾鏡頭延伸的原創內容

zh-tw.content:
她從上車到下車，只講了一句地址。

計程車的暖氣往擋風玻璃上吹，收音機放著一首二十年前的歌，司機小聲跟著哼副歌。

窗外那家店把鐵門拉到一半，兩個店員蹲在門口分一碗湯，紅綠燈在濕掉的柏油路上暈開。

到了以後她沒有馬上開門，等那首歌唱完才說了聲謝謝。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合形容累到說不出話的那種夜晚，情緒都藏在窗外的東西裡
variations: 短版：她什麼都沒說，那首歌幫她說完了。
延伸：最累的夜晚，通常安靜得像一段風景。

en.content:
From the moment she got in to the moment she got out, the address was the only thing she said.

The cab's heater pushed warm air at the windshield, the radio played something from twenty years ago, and the driver hummed the chorus under his breath.

Outside, a shop was pulling its shutter halfway down, two employees crouched by the door sharing a bowl of soup, and the traffic light bled across the wet asphalt.

When they pulled up she didn't reach for the handle, she waited for the song to end before saying thank you.
en.editorNote: For the kind of night when you're too tired to talk, everything you feel is out the window
variations: Short: she said nothing, the song on the radio said it for her.
Try this: the heaviest nights are quiet enough to look like scenery.

items.sourceNote: Marie Claire 台灣版2026韓劇推薦專題，追劇族心理側寫，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
剛下跑步機，你上次講的那部我追到第十集了（刪掉）
你會不會覺得我很煩（刪掉）
置物櫃號碼我按成你的生日，連開錯兩次別人的櫃子（刪掉）
擦汗的時候突然很想跟你說話（太肉麻，刪掉）
沒事啦，就是想問你最近好不好（太假，刪掉）
第十集那一句，我想拿來跟你講很久了（刪掉）
週三老時間，我在這裡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個草稿匣比對話紀錄還長的人——或是傳給幫你按住手機的那個朋友
variations: 更短的版本：草稿有七句，送出去的那句最普通，但只有它會在對方手機裡響一聲。

en.content:
Just off the treadmill, I'm on episode ten of the one you mentioned (deleted)
Am I being annoying (deleted)
I punched your birthday into the locker keypad and opened someone else's twice (deleted)
Wiping my face and suddenly wanted to talk to you (too much, deleted)
Nothing, just wondering how you've been (too fake, deleted)
There's a line in episode ten I've wanted to say to you for months (deleted)
Wednesday, same time. I'll be here.
en.editorNote: For the person whose drafts folder is longer than the actual thread — or for the friend holding their phone
variations: Shorter: seven drafts, one sent. The plainest one was the only one that made a sound on the other end.

items.sourceNote: Korean Binge英文韓劇金句整理站，離別場景語感參考，原創改編

zh-tw.content: 我在二手書店第三排找到那本你翻爛的劇本書，扉頁上還留著你寫的集數和播出時間。你把第七集那一頁折了角，旁邊用鉛筆寫著這裡不要快轉。店家在封底貼了六十元的標籤，我沒有告訴他這本書在我家床頭躺過兩年。我把它買回來了，那個折角我沒有攤平。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合寫給那個把你們的東西整理掉的人，也適合寫給還整理不掉的自己
variations: 延伸版本：同一排還有第二本一樣的，我沒買，因為那本沒有折角。

en.content: I found the script book you wore out, third shelf in from the door of the used bookstore, your handwriting still on the flyleaf with episode numbers and air times. You dog-eared the page for episode seven and wrote in pencil beside it, don't skip this part. The shop stuck a sixty-dollar tag on the back cover, and I didn't tell them it spent two years on my nightstand. I bought it back, and I left the fold exactly where you put it.
en.editorNote: For the person who cleared out everything you shared — or for the version of you that still can't
variations: There was a second copy on the same shelf. I left it there. No fold in that one.

items.sourceNote: udnSTYLE八月新劇追劇報導，觀眾情緒反應側寫，原創改編

zh-tw.content: 排隊等自助洗車的那十幾分鐘，我眼睛紅得像剛跟人大吵一架，前面那台車的駕駛還特地倒回來問我要不要先洗。他大概以為我的車被誰刮了，往壞處想一點，以為我是被丟下的那一個。把我弄成那樣的，是等泡沫噴完的四分鐘裡，我用手機看完了一部劇的最後三分鐘。我對他揮揮手說沒事，然後坐回車上，把那三分鐘又重看了一遍。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個也在很奇怪的地方哭過的追劇同好，互相認證一下
variations: 延伸版本：後照鏡裡我的臉還在抖，泡沫倒是已經沖乾淨了，只好投錢再洗一次。

en.content: Fifteen minutes in line at the self-serve car wash and my eyes were red enough that the driver ahead backed up to offer me his bay. He probably figured someone had keyed my door, or worse, that I'd just been left by somebody. What did it was the four-minute foam cycle, which turned out to be exactly long enough for the last three minutes of a show on my phone. I waved him off, got back in the car, and watched those three minutes again.
en.editorNote: Send it to the friend who has also cried somewhere ridiculous because of a drama
variations: Follow-up: my face was still going in the rearview but the foam was gone, so I paid for a second wash.

items.sourceNote: TALKace韓劇金句專題，家人共看情境參考，原創改編

zh-tw.content:
媽：你昨天看到第幾集了？
我：十四集，男主角躺在醫院那邊。
媽：那一段你不要看，看了晚上會睡不著。
我：你上禮拜在這裡唱歌唱到一半也在擦眼睛。
媽：那是電風扇一直對著我吹。
我：星期四這間沒排課，投影機借得到。
媽：椅子我搬，你負責把那台機器接好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個嘴上說不看、每次卻默默坐到最後一排看完的家人
variations: 延伸版本：星期四那天她提早四十分鐘到，說她只是來擦椅子。

en.content:
Mom: What episode are you on?
Me: Fourteen. The one where he's in the hospital.
Mom: Skip that part, you won't sleep.
Me: You were wiping your eyes halfway through your song in this room last week.
Mom: The fan was blowing right at me.
Me: Nobody booked this room for Thursday. We can borrow the projector.
Mom: I'll move the chairs, you figure out the cables.
en.editorNote: For the relative who claims they don't watch it and still takes the back row every single time
variations: Thursday she turned up forty minutes early. Said she only came to wipe down the chairs.

items.sourceNote: 驗光流程與常見迷思說明；由追劇族進驗光室的心虛感延伸的原創內容

zh-tw.content:
【成就解鎖】看清楚了
達成條件：在驗光室裡把那排小字唸到最後一行
附加獎勵：證實昨晚眼睛紅腫的原因與度數無關
隱藏條件：驗光師問你一天用眼多久，你答不出十四集要幾小時
稱號更新：戴新鏡片的人
提示：換一副眼鏡並不會讓你看懂他為什麼要走
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合追劇追到眼睛壞掉、去配眼鏡時心虛的人，貼在限動配一張驗光單剛好
variations: 短版：成就達成——把視力表唸完了，把那句台詞還是沒看懂。
延伸：新鏡片很清楚，模糊的部分本來就不在眼睛裡。

en.content:
ACHIEVEMENT UNLOCKED: 20/20
Requirement: read the smallest line in the exam chair all the way to the end
Bonus: confirmed last night's swollen eyes had nothing to do with your prescription
Hidden clause: the optometrist asks about your screen time and you can't say fourteen episodes
Title updated: Person With New Lenses
Note: a sharper lens still won't explain why he left
en.editorNote: For anyone who wrecked their eyes bingeing and felt caught out at the optician's
variations: Short: achievement unlocked — finished the eye chart, still can't read that line.
Try this: the new lenses are sharp. The blurry part was never in your eyes.

items.sourceNote: 2026 治癒系韓劇台詞整理；由自習室閉館前偷看一集的情境延伸的原創內容

zh-tw.content:
【第三關：閉館前二十分鐘】
目標：把耳機裡那一集聽完，手要放在原文書上
障礙：日光燈分區熄滅，你這一排永遠最先暗
道具：冰塊融光的美式，吸管咬到扁掉
失敗條件：館員來收桌時聽見你吸鼻子
通關獎勵：走出大門那一刻，夜風剛好把臉吹乾
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個一邊唸書一邊偷追劇的朋友，考季限定的共犯感
variations: 短版：通關條件很簡單，走出大門以前把臉吹乾就好。
延伸：那一排燈先暗不是巧合，是給你留一點時間。

en.content:
STAGE 3: TWENTY MINUTES TO CLOSING
Objective: finish the episode in your earbuds, keep one hand on the textbook
Hazard: the lights go out by section and your row always goes first
Item: an iced americano melted to water, straw chewed flat
Fail condition: the librarian hears you sniff while clearing the desks
Clear reward: the night air outside dries your face on the way down the steps
en.editorNote: Send it to the friend who studies with one earbud in and a drama in the other
variations: Short: clear condition is simple — get your face dry before you reach the door.
Try this: your row goes dark first on purpose. Somebody's giving you a minute.

items.sourceNote: 2026 韓劇片單報導；由包廂裡放片頭曲的追劇習慣延伸的原創內容

zh-tw.content:
報修單 0822　包廂 K7 點歌機
客戶描述：畫面跳到韓劇片頭就整台當掉
現場檢查：機器正常，是客人自己按了暫停，按了四次
處理方式：陪唱兩首，把面紙盒推過去
零件更換：無
備註：她下次再訂這間，燈先調暗，遙控器放她那邊
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合寫給那種不多問、只是把面紙推過來的人，也適合當店員視角的溫柔
variations: 短版：機器沒壞，壞的那位已經自己按暫停四次了。
延伸：報修單上寫無需更換零件，備註欄寫了三行。

en.content:
TICKET 0822 — Room K7, song console
Reported issue: unit freezes whenever a K-drama opening comes up
On-site check: console fine. Guest hit pause herself. Four times.
Action taken: sang two songs with her, slid the tissue box over
Parts replaced: none
Note: next time she books K7, dim the lights first and leave her the remote
en.editorNote: For the person who doesn't ask questions and just moves the tissues closer
variations: Short: nothing wrong with the machine. The one who kept hitting pause, though.
Try this: parts replaced, none. The notes field ran three lines long.

items.sourceNote: 2026 韓劇盤點報導；由深夜濱海公路返程的追劇餘韻延伸的原創內容

zh-tw.content:
以下為週五夜間路況播報
濱海公路南下順暢，海風偏強，建議車窗開一半就好
第十七公里處視線良好，沒有任何理由靠邊停車
若您在此路段忽然想起某一句對白，屬正常現象
後座乘客已睡著，播放清單將自動續播至終點
本時段由一句還沒說出口的話為您贊助播出
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合深夜開車回家、腦袋裡還在跑最後一集的時候發限動
variations: 短版：路況良好，沒有任何理由靠邊停，但我還是停了三分鐘。
延伸：後座那位睡著了，副歌只好由我一個人唱完。

en.content:
FRIDAY NIGHT TRAFFIC REPORT
Coastal highway southbound is clear, sea wind strong, window halfway down is plenty
Visibility good at kilometer seventeen, no reason whatsoever to pull over
If a line of dialogue surfaces along this stretch, that is normal
Backseat passenger is asleep, playlist will keep going to the exit
This segment brought to you by something still unsaid
en.editorNote: For the drive home at midnight with the finale still running in your head
variations: Short: road's clear, no reason to pull over. I pulled over for three minutes anyway.
Try this: he fell asleep back there, so I had to take the chorus alone.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 8 月韓劇開播清單報導；由「寄還東西」這個韓劇常見橋段延伸的原創對話，非引用任何劇中台詞

zh-tw.content:
「這件寄台南，姓陳的那位收。」
「要保價嗎？」
「外套不用，裡面那張紙條麻煩幫我保。」
「紙條上寫了什麼，要幫您封起來嗎？」
「封起來就好——我自己看了三年也沒看懂」
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合話卡在喉嚨很久的人；當「寄出去」比「說出口」還容易的時候，可以配這段發限動
variations: 短版：外套不用保價，裡面那張紙條要。
延伸：櫃檯小姐沒有多問，只是把膠帶撕得比平常慢一點。

en.content:
"This one goes to Tainan, to a Mr. Chen."
"Insuring it?"
"The coat can travel bare. The folded note inside, please insure that one."
"Should I seal it up for you?"
"Seal it. I've read it for three years and I still can't tell what it means."
en.editorNote: For anyone who's been holding a sentence in their throat too long; mailing it is easier than saying it
variations: Short: the coat doesn't need insuring. The note folded inside it does.
Try this: the clerk asked nothing else. She just tore the tape a little slower than usual.

items.sourceNote: 2026 韓劇片單推薦報導；由韓劇常見的「旁觀他人其實在看自己」視角延伸的原創內容

zh-tw.content:
夜市那攤射氣球前面站著一個人，槍已經舉了很久，卻遲遲沒有扣下去。
老闆說再打不中就直接送她一支娃娃，她搖頭，說要自己打到。
連續三輪，氣球一顆都沒破，倒是把後面排隊的人都等到隔壁攤去了。
她終於把槍放下，跟老闆說謝謝，轉身的時候我在攤位那面招牌玻璃上看見了自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合明知道可以放手、卻硬要自己完成的那種倔強；寫給還在原地重打第四輪的人
variations: 短版：老闆說要送她，她說她要自己打到。第三輪結束，隊伍已經散了。
延伸：轉身那一秒才發現，招牌玻璃上映出來的是我。

en.content:
At the balloon-shooting stall there's a woman who has been holding the rifle up for a very long time without firing.
The owner offers to just hand her a prize; she shakes her head and says she wants to win it herself.
Three rounds in, not one balloon has popped, and the line behind her has quietly drifted to the next stall.
She finally sets the rifle down and thanks him, and as she turns I catch my own face in the stall's glass sign.
en.editorNote: For the stubborn kind who could take the shortcut and refuse to; still reloading for round four
variations: Short: he offered to hand it to her. She said she'd rather earn it. The line behind her gave up first.
Try this: the second she turned around, I recognized the face in the glass.

items.sourceNote: 2026 治癒系韓劇金句整理；由「忍住的眼淚」情緒母題延伸的原創物件視角內容，未引用原文台詞

zh-tw.content:
我是驗光機裡那顆熱氣球，一天要被幾百個人盯著看，久了誰在忍什麼我大概分得出來。
今天下午那位小姐把額頭靠上來的時候，我腳下那片草原突然整個糊掉，機器判定是她眼睛在動。
她眨了兩下，說是冷氣太強，然後很快把臉挪開。
我在她面前浮了三十秒，飄回原位，等下一個假裝什麼事都沒發生的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種在外面撐住、只有機器知道的瞬間；也適合配一張很日常的照片發文
variations: 短版：草原糊掉的那一秒，機器判定是眼睛在動。
延伸：她說是冷氣太強。我浮在那裡，什麼都沒說。

en.content:
I'm the hot-air balloon inside the autorefractor, and after a few hundred foreheads a day you learn to tell who is holding something in.
When the woman this afternoon leaned her forehead against the rest, the meadow under my basket blurred all at once, and the machine logged it as eye movement.
She blinked twice, said the air conditioning was too strong, and pulled her face away quickly.
I hovered in front of her for thirty seconds, drifted back to my spot, and waited for the next person pretending nothing had happened.
en.editorNote: For the moment you hold it together in public and only a machine notices
variations: Short: the meadow blurred, and the machine called it eye movement.
Try this: she blamed the air conditioning. I just floated there and said nothing.

items.sourceNote: 韓劇金句整理報導；由韓劇常見的「剪頭髮＝重新開始」慢鏡頭語彙延伸的原創內容

zh-tw.content:
設計師問要剪多少，她抬起手，在鏡子裡比出一個大概到肩膀的位置，比完卻沒有把手放下來。
那隻手就停在半空中，像在確認自己真的可以做這個決定。
剪刀第一次合起來的時候，她盯著鏡子，看那截頭髮從肩膀滑下去，落在圍布上，沒有發出任何聲音。
她這才把手放下，說再短一點也沒關係。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合真的準備要往前走的那天；比任何宣言都適合當「我沒事了」的貼文
variations: 短版：她比完長度，手卻停在半空中沒放下來。
延伸：頭髮落在圍布上，一點聲音都沒有。她說再短一點也沒關係。

en.content:
The stylist asks how much to take off, and she lifts a hand to the mirror to mark a line around her shoulder, then leaves the hand hanging there.
It stays up in the air, as if she's checking whether she's really allowed to make this call.
The first time the scissors close she watches the mirror as a length of hair slides off her shoulder and lands on the cape without a sound.
Only then does she lower her hand and say a little shorter would be fine too.
en.editorNote: For the day you're actually ready to move on; better than any announcement post
variations: Short: she marked the length, then left her hand hanging in the air.
Try this: the hair landed on the cape without a sound. She said go shorter.
